results.name: Navigate Clio Manage
results.title: Navigate Clio Manage
results.body:
Clio Manage is a practice management software where you can manage your law firm clients, cases, files, billing, payments, and much more. After signing up for Clio Manage, you can begin setting up your account. Take a look at the resources below to learn more about navigating the Clio Manage interface.

Tip: Learn more about setting up Clio Manage here.

Header

Across the top of your Clio Manage interface is your home for all quick access items. From your header you can search using the global search bar, view recently viewed contacts and matters, start a billing timer, and create new assets. The header will also show you your notifications, which can be managed in your settings.

 

Side navigation bar

Use the navigation bar to access case-specific files and resources for your account. When you click each tab, you will see a header with subtabs for navigating actions in the section and a table for navigating and manipulating data. Clio Manage contains the following tabs:

Dashboard

Personal Dashboard

Firm Dashboard, Organization Dashboard

Firm Feed

Personal Dashboard

The Personal Dashboard gives you a snapshot of pertinent information related to your overall personal and specific matters and includes the following:

  • Today's Agenda: This section shows your tasks that are due today and your calendar events for the day.
  • Hourly Metrics: This section shows your target billable time compared to the actual billable time that you logged. Non-billable time will not appear as part of this metric. You can set your personal performance targets for this metric in your settings. See the "Set up personal performance target" section here to learn more.
  • Billing Metrics for Firm: This section shows the number of bills and value amount totals that you have in each bill state. You can only view this section if you are an administrator or if you have billing and reports permissions, and if your billing rate visibility is not restricted.
  • Financial Metrics: This section shows billed and unbilled time entered in Clio for the fiscal year, plotted relative to the annual performance targets. The calculations in each graph are based on a 260-day year to account for weekends. You can only view this section if you are an administrator or if you have billing and reports permissions, and if your billing rate visibility is not restricted.
  • Detailed Annual Report: This report shows a visual of your personal performance metrics. It displays the target billable time you aimed to reach by the end of the year compared to the actual billable time you logged for the year. You can only view this section if you are an administrator or if you have billing and reports permissions, and if your billing rate visibility is not restricted. Learn more here.
Firm Dashboard

The Firm Dashboard offers managers, administrators, and users with reporting permissions insights into the utilization, realization, and collection metrics of their firms. It presents data by your desired year and can be adjusted with the date selector at the top of the page. This dashboard calculates all metrics based on the date of an activity, not the date of a payment or bill. 

  • Utilization: The utilization rate is a measure of productivity and shows how much of the day is spent doing billable work in comparison to the available hours in a day (Clio uses an eight-hour available work day). It is calculated as the billable hours worked divided by the available working hours (in the number of days in a month). Each user's working days are defined by the values set for their personal performance target.
  • Realization: The realization rate is a measure of value efficiency and shows the amount of billable work recorded that is actually put on a bill, excluding any discounts. It is calculated as the total number of billed hours subtracted by the discounted hours and then divided by the total number of billable hours worked.
  • Collection: The collection rate shows how much of the firm's billed work clients have paid for. It is calculated as the total amount of hours collected divided by the total number of non-discounted hours billed.
Firm Feed

The firm feed allows you to monitor account activity and events for the firm (e.g., creating matters and contacts, recording payments, updating bills, creating, editing, and deleting time and expense entries, changing user permissions, uploading documents, and much more). Filters help narrow the view by user, type, and whether an activity or event was deleted or exported. 

Important: The Firm Feed is only visible to users with the Administrator role by default. To grant other users access, create a custom role, enable the View account firm feed permission in Firm Settings, and assign that role to them.

Available Type filters include the following:

  • Calendar: Filter by calendar entries, entry types, and membership types.
  • Tasks: Filter by task types.
  • Matter: Filter by bills, matter stages, trust requests, notes, permissions, and protected funds.
  • Contacts: Filter by people, companies, contact notes, client bills, and trust requests.
  • Clio for Co-Counsel: Filter by co-counsel permissions.
  • Activities: Filter by time entries, expense entries, and hard or soft costs. The row for a newly created Time Entry will display the start time when the timer is used. Look for the line that states [user name] created Time Entry, about [time] ago. The timestamp on the right will display the exact date and time the timer was started. You can also track updates to the entry, which appear as new rows when you select a matter or change the activity description.

  • Exports: Filter to view a log of export events for matter list exports, contact list exports, and activity list exports. Admin exports performed through the Admin Export Page are not logged in the Firm Feed.

    Note: The firm feed will only include export events that occur after Jan. 15, 2025.
  • Bills: Filter by payments and interest.
  • Online Payments: Filter by merchant account mapping and Clio Payments.
  • Accounts: Filter by refunds, trust request payments, and refunds.
  • Communication: Filter by conversations, messages, emails, and phone calls.
  • Documents: Filter by document versions and signature requests.
  • Settings: Filter by payment profiles, users, recovery events, invitations, and logins.
  • Personal injury: Filter by personal injury settings, damages, and liens.

  • Role membership: Filter by user permission changes.

    Note: The firm feed will only include permission change events that occur after Apr. 8, 2025.

If your firm uses multiple currencies, you can use the currency dropdown in the Personal Dashboard and Firm Dashboard to view the metrics for currencies other than the firm’s default currency.

Calendar

In this tab, you can navigate how you view your calendars, change months, and change date views. You can also add new calendar events, as well as share and modify calendar preferences. Learn more about calendars here.

Tasks

In this tab, you can view tasks depending on whether they are outstanding or completed tasks, search by date range, and filter results further. You can also manage task types, task lists, task feeds, and create new tasks. Learn more about tasks here.

Matters

In this tab, you can view matters by matter status (open, pending, closed), search through matters quickly and easily with a keyword search, add or remove columns, filter the table view, and add new matters. Learn more about matters here.

Contacts

In this tab, you can view contacts by contact type (person or company contacts), search through contacts quickly and easily with a keyword search, add or remove columns, filter the table view, and add new contacts. Learn more about contacts here.

Activities

In this tab, you can view activities by time or expense entries, sort by date range, search through activities quickly and easily with a keyword search, add or remove columns, and filter the table view. You can also manage activity categories and add new time and expense entries. Learn more about activities here.

Billing

In this tab, you can view current or outstanding bills and further differentiate bills by bill state, search through bills quickly and easily with a bill ID search, add or remove columns, and filter the table view. You can also record payments on bills and generate new bills. Learn more about bills here.

Online payments

In this tab, you can view a transaction history for clients by all clients, authorized transactions, completed transactions, and failed transactions. You can also view existing payment plans by all plans, active plans, stopped plans, and completed plans for which bills have been fully paid, and create new payment plans and new transaction charges. Learn more about payments here.

Accounts

In this tab, you can view your connected bank accounts, export account information, create new bank accounts, add or remove columns, and filter the table view. Learn more about bank accounts here.

Documents

In this tab, you can view documents stored in Clio Manage and documents from connected third-party document applications by both files and folders or only files. You can also search through documents quickly and easily with a keyword search, add or remove columns, filter the table view, upload new documents, and connect Clio's cloud-based document management application, Clio Drive. Learn more about documents here and Clio Drive here.

E-filings

In this tab, firms in Texas or Georgia who enable Clio File can view electronic filings by submission status or e-filing status. You can also create new filings, edit drafts, and cancel submissions. To learn more about e-filing with Clio, see Clio File: E-File and E-Serve Documents.

Communications

In this tab, you will find an inbox-style display that allows you to add new communications, reply to messages, and navigate through existing conversations and communication logs. You can quickly click through different communication channels and use subtabs to sort data by owner or type. Within each communication channel, you can sort by date or alphabetically, as well as filter and search using keywords. Learn more about communications here.

Reports

Get unique insights into all aspects of how your firm is performing. Reports can be filtered by categories, with details of what will be pulled on screen. Learn more about reports here.

App Integrations

  • Home: The Clio App directory is a quick way to explore the apps available to make your Clio account unique to your needs. Learn more about integrations here.
  • Search: Want to make your Clio experience even better? Do a keyword search for what you are looking for and add the integration that is right for you.
  • My Integrations: Click this tab to find a list of your active integrations.

Settings

In this tab, you can set up, enable, and disable various Clio Manage settings. Learn more here.

 

Resource center

  • Offers: Curious about Clio product offers and promotions? Check out this section in your side panel for more details on what Clio is offering right now. 
  • Help Center: The Help Center is Clio's knowledge base for getting answers to your product and workflow questions. Quickly and easily access a breadth of learning materials right from this side panel.
  • Law Community: The Law Community is a place for Clio customers to connect with each other, offer support, answer questions, and help each other be more successful. This is a dedicated place to meet other innovative and passionate legal professionals like yourself. 

Important: If you cannot log in to the Law Community using your Clio credentials, sign up for your community account using the create an account option located on the login window. The following users will not be able to access the community using their Clio credentials and should use the create an account option when logging in for the first time.

  • Accounts that are less than two weeks old.
  • Customers who are still in trial.
  • Customers with accounts hosted on our European or Canadian servers.
  • Customers who use the mobile two-factor push notification feature.

results.name: Accounting Dashboard
results.title: Accounting Dashboard
results.body:
Regularly reviewing your firm's financial situation and accounting health is an important part of running your business. Not only can this help you spot discrepancies easier and remain compliant, but getting an overview of unpaid client invoices, monthly expenses, net change of money in and money out, and net income and expenses is a key part of running a successful business. 

 

Navigate the dashboard

Your firm's Dashboard provides a bird's eye view of your firm's financial status, allowing you to view trends quickly and get an understanding of your firm's financial health. It includes the following sections:

Firm accounts:

This section shows a summary view of your operating, trust, and credit card bank accounts. For each account, you can view the running balance in Clio Accounting and the number of new bank transactions that need to be reviewed (categorized and matched). Click the three dots next to a bank account's name and select Review transactions to start the bank feed review. 

Accounts receivable:

This section shows the running balance of your accounts receivable (i.e. the total outstanding balance from all outstanding client invoices), the number of invoices that have been fully paid in the current month, and the number of total invoices with amounts owing to date. Click View to go to the Accounts receivable tab, where you can view outstanding balances by client. 

Operating expenses: 

This section shows this month's operating expenses and the percentage change compared to the previous month. Click View to go to the Operating expenses tab to view your firm's created, matched, and reconciled operating expenses.

Hard costs:

This section shows you the hard costs for review, and any yet to be invoiced. Click Review to go to the Hard Costs tab, where you can view invoiced and to be invoiced hard costs. When reviewing hard costs, click the blue text to go to the corresponding area in Manage.

Profit and loss:

This section shows the net income (income minus expenses), total income, and expenses for the last two months. Click View to go to the corresponding report. 

Accounting best practices:

This section provides accounting tips, with weekly and monthly checklists that highlight key accounting tasks. This tool is designed to help you get a better understanding of accounting and how to stay on top of your books each week and each month. 

Recommended tasks:

If you did not yet complete all the recommended actions for setting up Clio Accounting in order to get started, this section will appear at the top of your dashboard with your next suggested actions.

results.name: Roles and Permissions in Clio Manage
results.title: Roles and Permissions in Clio Manage
results.body:
Clio Manage offers flexible options for managing user permissions through system standard roles and custom roles. You will need to assign every firm user a role. These roles control what users see and do within Clio Manage, ensuring they have the correct access level to perform their duties efficiently while protecting confidential client data. 

Important: Users with multiple roles inherit the permissions from the most permissive role.
Tip: Learn more about permissions in Clio Grow here.

Understand standard roles and custom roles

In Clio Manage, you can choose from five standard roles or create custom roles to fit your firm's unique needs. Standard roles are a great starting point for new firms, and you can use them as templates for custom roles. The sections below outline the core functions of each standard role and the non-configurable permissions.

Note: Non-configurable permissions are built into standard roles and carry over when you use them as a template for a custom role.

Administrator

Assign this role to firm users, managing partners, or anyone who requires full access to all firm settings, user management, and data. Administrators have maximum access, resulting in several non-configurable permissions. 

Important: The Firm Feed is only visible to users with the Administrator role by default. To give other users access, create a custom role, and enable the View account firm feed permission under the Firm Settings section. You can assign roles immediately after creation.

What an Administrator can do:

  • Manage contacts, matters, and documents.
  • View all firm activities and financial information.
  • Manage users and roles.
  • Access and configure all firm settings.
Non-configurable permissions
  • Accounts: View, create, edit, delete, export, and manage transactions and bank accounts.
  • Activities: View all categories, bulk edit bills, and billed items.
  • Calendars: Manage all calendars
  • Conflict Checks: Create, view, and manage conflict checks. Administrators can also view the conflict check report, bypassing matter and contact visibility permissions
  • Dashboard: View firm dashboard
  • Documents: Unlock user-locked documents
  • Matters: Administer stages and templates, manage billing preferences, and block users.
  • Payments: Manage Clio Payments, including payment plans and charges. Admins can also administer merchant accounts, view tax forms, and sign up.
  • Reports: View, create, download, and manage report presets and schedules.
  • Settings: Manage bill syncs, billing, documents, expenses, firm settings, grants, and matter numbering.
  • Tasks: Manage, bulk edit, and bulk delete tasks.
  • Transactions: View, edit, export, and manage all transactions, including trust transactions.
  • Workflow Automations: Manage automated workflows.

 

Accounts

Assign this role to users who require access to the trust and operating account and will record transactions. You can view the default and non-configurable permissions below. 

What the Accounts role can do:

  • Manage matter financials.
  • View activities from assigned matters
Non-configurable permissions
  • Accounts: View, create, edit, delete, export, and manage transactions and bank accounts.
  • Matters: Manage billing preferences.
  • Transactions: Export and manage trusts.

 

General Access

Assign this role to most legal professionals, such as lawyers and paralegals. This role provides a strong baseline for managing matters, tracking time, and working with clients. 

What the General Access role can do:

  • Contacts management
    • Edit, delete contacts, create contacts, and export contacts
  • Matter management
    • Edit matter properties, Delete matters, Create matters, Export matters, View matter timeline
  • Timekeeping
    • Views activities from assigned matters
Non-configurable permissions
  • Conflict checks: Create, view, and manage conflict checks

 

Billing

Assign this role to a bookkeeper or accounting staff member who primarily manages firm finances, including bill payments and account transactions. 

What the Billing role can do:

  • View matter financials
  • Views all activities
  • Create, manage, and view bills and trust requests.
Non-configurable permissions
  • Accounts: View bank accounts
  • Activities: Bulk edit
  • Matters: Manage billing preferences
  • Payments: Manage plans, create charges, and view tax forms.
  • Settings: Manage billing
  • Transactions: View, edit, and manage.

 

Reports

Assign this role to managers who need to run firm-wide reports to analyze data without requiring access to other administrative settings.

What the Reports role can do: 

  • View activities from assigned matters.
Non-configurable permissions
  • Dashboard: View firm dashboard
  • Reports: View, create, and download reports, report presets, and report schedules. 

 

When to use custom roles

Custom roles provide administrators precise control over user access to firm and client information. While Clio Manage’s system roles offer a solid foundation, custom roles enable tailored permission sets that meet your firm’s unique security, compliance, and workflow needs.

Note: This feature is available to select plans. Learn more about your plan's features. If you need to upgrade your firm’s plan, ask a firm administrator.

You may want to create custom roles for your firm to:

  • Define precise access and avoid over-privileging: Create a custom role to grant users access only to the data and functionalities they need. This directly addresses the need to avoid providing users with more access than their specific roles require, ensuring they have the correct tools for their tasks.
  • Maintain compliance and protect client information: Custom roles help enforce ethical obligations and professional rules of conduct regarding client confidentiality. Control access to records (for example, Contacts and bills) and enable record filtering. You can limit who can view, edit, delete, or export sensitive information. This reduces risk and maintains data integrity.
  • Streamline user management as your firm grows: For larger firms with many users, custom roles simplify the onboarding process. Instead of manually adjusting permissions for each new user, you can assign them a pre-configured role that matches their responsibilities.

 

Sample custom roles to get started

You can use standard roles as a baseline for managing your team. For more specific access, you can also create custom roles that are tailored to your firm’s unique needs. You can use a standard role as a template or build a new role from scratch. Here are some examples to help you get started: 

Partner

This role provides them with all the access they need to carry out their practice and stay focused.

Key permissions:

  • Edit and delete contacts
  • Edit matter properties
  • Create and delete matters
  • View matter timeline
  • View matter financials
  • View firm feed
  • View activities from assigned matters

 

Junior Paralegal

Create this role for a user who needs to perform daily tasks like managing matters and contacts while preventing them from taking sensitive administrative actions. 

Key permissions: 

  • Create matter, edit matter properties, view matter timeline
  • Create and edit contacts
  • View Own activities

 

Billing Manager

This role offers access to financial data and reporting without providing full administrator permissions. The Billing system role is a great template for this.

Key permissions:

  • Create and manage bills
  • View all activities
  • Perform bulk actions for transactions and accounts
  • Export matters

 

Accountant

This role grants an Accountant limited, read-only access to firm contacts and billing information. The Accounts system role is a good starting point for this custom role.

Key permissions:

  • View Own activities
  • View matter financials
  • View bills

results.name: Get Started With Matters
results.title: Get Started With Matters
results.body:
In Clio Manage, a matter is the file that holds a single legal case. Every piece of casework attaches to a matter, from time entries and documents to tasks and bills, so the full history of a case stays in one place. The Matters page lists every matter at your firm, and each matter opens onto its own dashboard and subtabs for the work attached to it.

Tip: Before adding matters, set up your matter numbering scheme. The numbering scheme defines how matter numbers and descriptions appear.

 

Navigate matter subtabs

Opening a single matter gives you every piece of matter-specific data in one place, organized into subtabs.

  1. Go to Matters.
  2. Find your matter and click the matter name.

 

The subtabs available on a matter depend on your firm's subscription and on your role. An administrator who limits billing permissions, or a firm without eFiling, changes which subtabs a user can open. Learn more about roles and permissions in Clio Manage.

Dashboard

An overview of the matter, including financials such as work in progress, outstanding balance, and matter trust funds. It also holds a Details section carrying the matter's core fields, including status, the open, pending, closed, and limitations dates, practice area, matter stage, and the responsible and originating attorney, plus contacts for clients and related contacts, custom fields, and conflict checks. Depending on your subscription, the dashboard also holds eFiling, Recent Vincent conversations, and AI Actions. Users can also customize which sections appear.

Clio Work

For firms with Clio Work, this subtab provides direct access to Vincent AI, Editor, Clio Library, and Clio Docket. Clio Work drafts proactive next steps specific to the matter in advance, ready for review on the matter dashboard. Firms with Clio Draft can also reach Clio Draft from here. This subtab opens Clio Work outside the matter.

Custom Fields

Holds matter custom fields, where you add fields and update field data. Learn more about custom fields in Clio Manage.

Activities

Holds the time entries and expenses recorded against the matter. Learn more about activities.

Calendar

Holds calendar events for the matter, defaulting to upcoming events, with options for past and all events. You can create events, manage visible columns, and search and filter the event table. Learn more about calendars.

Communications

Holds communications for the matter, including phone logs, email logs, text messages, internal firm messages, and messages shared with clients through the client portal. Learn more about communications.

Notes

Holds notes for the matter. Learn more about managing notes in Clio.

Documents

Holds documents for the matter, including documents held in third-party drives such as Google Drive. Learn more about documents.

eFiling

For firms with Clio File, this subtab holds documents eFiled and eServed to local courts for the matter, and tracks every submission. Learn more about eFiling.

Tasks

Holds tasks for the matter. Learn more about tasks.

Bills

Holds bills for the matter. Learn more about billing.

Transactions

Holds transactions for the matter, including payments, transferred funds, and trust request transactions. Learn more about payments and trust requests.

Clio for Co-Counsel

Holds resources shared with co-counsel on the matter. Learn more about Clio for Co-Counsel.

Medical Records

For firms with the Personal Injury add-on, this subtab holds medical provider cards, medical records, and medical bills for the matter. Learn more about medical records.

Damages

For firms with the Personal Injury add-on, this subtab holds the special and general damages recorded for the matter. Learn more about damages.

Settlement

For firms with the Personal Injury add-on, this subtab holds recovery amounts, deductions, and settlement statements for the matter. Learn more about settlement.

 

Up next

  • Add a matter: Create Matters. Set up a new matter, complete the matter form, and create placeholder matters for cases that are not yet confirmed.
  • Track a case through its lifecycle: Change Matter Statuses. Move a matter between open, pending, and closed as the case progresses.
  • Learn about matter statuses: Use matter statuses to keep your matters organized.

results.name: Damages
results.title: Damages
results.body:
In a personal injury matter, you need to keep track of your client's damages in order to help your client recover the cost of their injuries. Since personal injury cases can often take a long time to settle, you know how important it is to track damages in one central place. With Clio's Personal Injury Add-On, you can track various damages for a client directly within their matter file in Clio Manage and make changes at any time, allowing you to stay up-to-date on your client's case and collaborate with other members at your firm.

Note: This feature is a component of Clio's Personal Injury Add-On and is not available for all Clio subscription plans. See which plans have Clio's Personal Injury Add-On here. If you have questions about upgrading, contact Clio's support or sales teams here.

Tip: With the medical records component of Clio's Personal Injury Add-On, you can track medical providers, records, bills, and liens and outstanding balances. And with the settlement component, you can record proposed recovery amounts and your legal fees, and calculate your client's net recovery after deductions and legal fees. Learn more about tracking medical details here and settlement information here. 

Add new damages

You can add damages relevant to your client's case directly in their matter. This allows you to keep track of all damages for your personal injury matter in one place and view a running total of all damages for the matter. After adding damages in this subtab and medical bills in the Medical Records subtab (learn more about medical records here), you can view cards at the top of the Damages subtab that summarize totals for damages and medical bills, along with a medical bill summary of all medical bills recorded in the Medical Records subtab. 

  • Total billed and other damages: This card is the sum of the total of all medical bills recorded in the Medical Records subtab and the total of all damages recorded in the Damages subtab.
  • Total paid and other damages: This card is the sum of all paid medical bills recorded in the Medical Records subtab and the total of all damages recorded in the Damages subtab.
  • Total paid + owed and other damages: This card is the sum of all medical bill payments plus the outstanding balances owed to medical providers as recorded in the Medical Records and the total of all damages recorded in the Damages subtab.
  • Medical bills summary: This table shows a detailed summary of the medical bills added to a medical provider's card in the Medical Records subtab. The summarization will group the medical damages by provider with the total bill amount, any adjustments, the total paid, any balance owed, and any amount that is paid but still owed.

To add damages to the matter, follow the steps listed below:

  1. Go to your personal injury matter and select the Damages subtab.
  2. Click New damage.
  3. Enter a name or description for the damage, the amount, and then select the type of damage. 
  4. Click Save damage.
    • As you add more damages, you can view the total of all damages for the matter at the bottom of the table under the Amount column.
    • Your matter's Timeline and the Firm Feed will show when a damage was added and by which firm user. To access this matter's Timeline, click the Dashboard subtab in the matter's file. To access the Firm Feed, click the main Dashboard tab in the navigation menu on the left of your Clio Manage app. 

 

Edit damages

If you need to make any changes to a recorded damage, you can edit the type of damage, description, and amount directly from the matter's damages table.

  1. Go to the matter and select the Damages subtab.
  2. Optional: Select one of the quick filters to find the damage quicker. You can also enter a search term in the Filter by keyword box.
    • All: This quick filter shows all your recorded damages for the matter.
    • Special: This quick filter shows your recorded economic or pecuniary damages that can be clearly determined and compensate your client for their quantifiable financial losses, including reimbursement for medical bills, lost wages, future loss of earning capacity, etc. 
    • General: This quick filter shows your recorded non-economic or non-pecuniary damages that relate to the consequences of your client's injury rather than the injury itself and do not have a clear dollar value, including pain and suffering, lowered quality of life, loss of consortium/companionship, etc.
    • Other: This quick filter shows your recorded punitive, nominal, and aggravated damages for your client. 
  3. Under the Actions column, click the pencil icon.
  4. Make your changes and then click Save damage.
    • Your matter's Timeline and the Firm Feed will show when a damage was edited and by which firm user. To access this matter's Timeline, click the Dashboard subtab in the matter's file. To access the Firm Feed, click the main Dashboard tab in the navigation menu on the left of your Clio Manage app. 

 

Delete damages

You can delete individual damages for a matter from the matter's damages table. Once deleted, the damage cannot be recovered.  

  1. Go to the matter and select the Damages subtab.
  2. Optional: Select one of the quick filters to find the damage quicker. You can also enter a search term in the Filter by keyword box.
    • All: This quick filter shows all your recorded damages for the matter.
    • Special: This quick filter shows your recorded economic or pecuniary damages that can be clearly determined and compensate your client for their quantifiable financial losses, including reimbursement for medical bills, lost wages, future loss of earning capacity, etc. 
    • General: This quick filter shows your recorded non-economic or non-pecuniary damages that relate to the consequences of your client's injury rather than the injury itself and do not have a clear dollar value, including pain and suffering, lowered quality of life, loss of consortium/companionship, etc.
    • Other: This quick filter shows your recorded punitive, nominal, and aggravated damages for your client. 
  3. Under the Actions column, click either the pencil icon or the trash can icon.
  4. Select Delete damage.
    • Your matter's Timeline and the Firm Feed will show when a damage was deleted and by which firm user. To access this matter's Timeline, click the Dashboard subtab in the matter's file. To access the Firm Feed, click the main Dashboard tab in the navigation menu on the left of your Clio Manage app. 

 

Sort, filter, and export damages

From the damages table in the matter, you can sort your client's damages by damage type and amount, filter using a keyword search, and export damages as a CSV file. The export will show the damage type, description, and amount for each damages, along with the medical bill summary, which includes any adjustments, the total paid, any balance owing, and any medical bill amounts paid plus outstanding balances owed to medical providers. 

Tip: With Clio's Personal Injury Add-On, you can also run the damages export as a report, along with comprehensive reports for medical expenses and medical expense payments. Learn more about these reports here.

Sort

Tip: You can view the total of all damages for the matter at the bottom of the table under the Amount column.

  1. Go to the matter and select the Damages subtab.
  2. In the All other damages table, click the Type column to sort by damage type or click the Amount column to sort by damage amount in ascending or descending order. 
Filter
  1. Go to the matter and select the Damages subtab.
  2. In the All other damages table, select one of the quick filters to filter by type of damage. 
    • All: This quick filter shows all your recorded damages for the matter.
    • Special: This quick filter shows your recorded economic or pecuniary damages that can be clearly determined and compensate your client for their quantifiable financial losses, including reimbursement for medical bills, lost wages, future loss of earning capacity, etc.

results.name: Track and Manage Filings
results.title: Track and Manage Filings
results.body:
You can track and manage your firm's e-filings in Clio Manage. View filing statuses and details from the firm-wide e-filings dashboard, a matter dashboard or e-filing subtab. This article explains how to monitor filings, view rejection reasons, and court-stamped documents. As well as refile rejected documents, edit and delete drafts, and cancel submissions.

Monitor filing statuses

Once a filing is submitted, you can keep track of the status of the filing in Clio Manage. You can view the most recent filing status from the E-filings dashboard or matter's Dashboard or get a more in-depth view of all filing statuses for a matter in the matter's E-filing subtab. Filings can have one of the following statuses:

Draft

The filing has been created but has not been sent to the court's electronic filing manager (EFM).

Submitted

The filing has been successfully sent to the court's EFM.

Failed

The filing has not reached the court's EFM due to formatting errors.

Accepted

The filing has been approved by the court to proceed as an active matter.

Rejected

The filing has been denied by the court and deemed invalid for legal action. You can view the reason why the filing was rejected by viewing the filing submission in the matter's E-filing subtab, and then refile with the appropriate corrections.

Review Complete

The filing has been successfully reviewed by the court.

Canceled

The filing has been canceled by a firm user.

E-filings Matter Dashboard E-filing subtab
  1. Go to the main E-filings tab to view the firm-wide e-filing dashboard.
  2. Under Submissions, sort filings by Completed, Submitted, Draft, Canceled, or Failed submissions.
  3. Optional: Click the E-filings subtab to view all filings or Accepted, Rejected, Submitted, Draft, Canceled, and Failed filings. 
  4. View the status of filings under the Status column. 
  1. Go to the matter's Dashboard.
  2. In the E-filing box, view the status of each submitted filing and the submission date and time.
  3. Optional: Click View all to view all filings in the matter's E-filing subtab.
  1. Go to the matter and then select the E-filing subtab.
  2. View the status of the filing under the Status column. You can also click View to view a submitted filing.

 

View submitted filings, rejection reason, and court-stamped documents

Once you submit a filing, you can view the filing, including the payment summary and fee breakdown, from the matter's E-filing subtab. You can also view a description of why a filing was rejected from the same subtab. When the court accepts the filing, they will send court-stamped documents directly back to Clio Manage. You can view these documents in the matter's Documents subtab.

Note: If a court rejects a filing, you will need to start a new filing with the appropriate corrections. 

View submitted filingsView court-stamped documents
  1. Go to the matter and then select the E-filing subtab.
  2. Find the submitted filing that you want to view. You can use the keyword search box to help you find the filing.
  3. Under the Actions column of the table, click View.
  4. If the filing was rejected by the court, you can view the rejection reason in the Filing details section.
  1. Go to the matter and then select the Documents subtab.
  2. Find the documents that you want to view. You can use the keyword search box to help you find the document.
  3. Under the Actions column of the table, click View.

 

Refile rejected documents

If the court rejects a filing, you can use Clio File to easily resubmit your documents. The refiling submission date will reflect the actual date and time of your refiling, but the court clerk can assign the original docket date during their review.

Note: The court clerk reviewing the submission can change the docket date to reflect the original submission date and time. They do this by clicking Copy docket date during their review process. This ensures your filing history accurately reflects the original submission's docket date, even after a refile.
  1. Go to the main E-filings tab, you can also go to the matter and select the E-filing subtab.
  2. Locate the rejected filing.
  3. Under the Actions column, click the Refile icon next to rejected filings. Or, click the Eye icon to view the filing details, and click Refile (top right).
  4. View the Rejection reasons under Submission summary, make the appropriate changes, and submit the filing.

 

Edit and delete draft filings

If you saved a filing as a draft, you can continue to edit the draft filing or delete it. Be sure to thoroughly check the filing for accuracy before submitting it. Once you submit a filing, you cannot cancel it on your own and will instead need to contact Clio's support team for any cancellations. 

Edit draft filing Delete draft filing
  1. Go to the main E-filings tab or the matter's Dashboard.
  2. Find the draft filing that you want to edit.
  3. Under the Actions column of the table, click Edit.
  4. Make any necessary changes and then submit the filing.
  1. Go to the main E-filings tab or the matter's Dashboard.
  2. Find the draft filing that you want to delete.
  3. Under the Actions column of the table, click the arrow next to Edit and then select Delete.
  4. Click Delete draft to confirm the action.

 

Cancel filing submission

You can cancel recent submissions from the E-filing subtab in a matter, or when viewing the filings. You cannot cancel filings in review or previously reviewed by the courts. Once canceled, you will not be charged for the filing.

Note: Self-serve cancellation is currently available for Clio File submissions in Georgia and Texas. In California, self-serve cancellation is not yet supported. You will need to contact Clio Support for assistance with pending filings. For a full list of supported counties, see View available courts.

  1. Go to the main E-filings tab. You can also go to the matter and select the E-filing subtab.
  2. Find the filings you need to cancel.
  3. Click the X icon. You can also cancel submissions when viewing the filing.
  4. Click Cancel submission.
  5. In the pop-up modal, click Cancel submission to confirm.

results.name: Overview of Custom Role Permissions
results.title: Overview of Custom Role Permissions
results.body:
With Clio you can create custom roles and apply specific permissions to these roles to ensure that every user in your firm has the right access to the information they need and the ability to take the necessary actions in Clio. Review the information below to understand what level of access you can control and apply when you create a custom role.

Important: When you enable a permission that depends on others, Clio enables those automatically and shows a confirmation listing what changed. Select Undo change in that message if you don't want the dependent permissions enabled.

Contacts management

Contact management permissions control a user's ability to view and manage contacts, as well as define what actions a user can perform with them.

  • Create contacts: Allows users to add a new contact, person, or company to their firm.

    Note: Enabling Create contacts will also enable the Edit contacts permission.
  • Edit contacts: Allows users to edit contact properties like type, name, contact information, address, tags, custom fields, employees, and billing preferences

  • Delete contacts: Allows users to remove a single contact record from the system. A deleted contact can be recovered by the system administrator.

    Note: Enabling Delete contacts will also enable the Edit contacts permission.

    • Bulk delete contacts: Allow users to remove multiple contacts simultaneously.

      Note: Enabling Bulk delete contacts will also enable Delete contacts.
  • Export contacts: Enables the exporting of the firm's contacts via a PDF or CSV file.
  • Send review requests: Allows users to send a review request.

 

Matter management

Matter management permissions control user access to matters and all associated information, including documents, notes, communications, and activities. You can define which roles can view, edit, create, delete, and export matter-related information. This ensures data integrity and appropriate matter access for each user role. These permissions define what a user can do with matters.

  • Create matters: Allows users to create a new matter.
  • Edit matter properties: Allow users to edit properties for a single matter.

    • Bulk edit matters: Allow users to edit multiple matters simultaneously.

      Note: Enabling Bulk edit matters will also enable the Edit matter properties permission.

  • Delete matters: Allows users to delete a matter.

    Important: Deleting a matter is a permanent action.
    Note: Enabling Delete matters will also enable the Edit matter properties permission.
    • Bulk delete matters: Allow users to delete multiple matters simultaneously.
  • Export Matters: Allow users to export matters in PDF or CSV format.
  • View matter timeline: Allow users to see a chronological view of all activities and updates related to a specific matter. This includes actions like document uploads, time entries, and stage changes, located in the matter dashboard.
  • View restricted matters: Views high-level info for matters the user cannot access.
  • View matter financials: Allow users read-only access to the financial overview section on the matter dashboard, including, work in progress balance, outstanding balance, matter trust funds balance, matter budget (Billable and Non-billable).

 

Timekeeping

Timekeeping permissions control a user's access to activities and expenses.

View Activities

  • View all activities: Allow users to view all activities.
  • View activities from accessible matters: Allow users to view all activities for matters they own or have access to.
  • View own activities: Allow users to view their own activities only.

Manage Activities

  • Manage all activities: Allow users to manage all activities.
  • View activities from accessible matters: Allow users to manage all activities for matters they own or have access to.
  • View own activities: Allow users to manage their own activities only.

 

Financial management

Financial permissions control access to bills, transactions, and accounts. These permissions are critical for custom roles as they determine a user's access to financial subtabs (e.g., Transactions and Bills) within a matter or contact card. These permissions determine a user's access to financial actions and details of your firm's finances.

 

Accounts

Accounts permission allows users to see account information based on the following three levels:

  • All bank accounts: Includes all accounts in the firm, account balances, and account properties. Enables access to accounts in the global navigation.
  • Limited: Display account names and essential details for managing transactions and bills without displaying balances. Does not enable access to accounts in the global navigation.

  • None: Does not see any account information.

    Note: Selecting None will disable the Manage bills and trust requests and View transactions permissions.

 

Transactions

  • View transactions: Allows users to see the Transactions tab within a Matter or Contact card. This permission is required for users to view trust account activity and retainer balances.

    Note: To view transactions, the user also needs at minimum the Limited view of bank account information permission for Accounts.

 

Bills and trust requests

  • View bills and trust requests: Allow users to view the Bills section in the left navigation and the Bills tab in Matters and Contacts, as well as viewing, quick viewing, downloading, and printing bills and copying links to bills.

    Granular billing permissions within this option include allowing this permission for All bills & trust requests or limiting this permission to Accessible matters or Responsible attorney. Select None to prevent the user from viewing any bills or trust requests.

  • Manage draft bills and trust requests: Allow users to edit and delete draft bills and trust requests, and submit them for approval.

    Granular billing permissions within this option include allowing this permission for All bills & trust requests or limiting this permission to Accessible matters or Responsible attorney. Select None to prevent the user from managing any draft bills or trust requests.

    Note: Enabling this permission will also enable the same access level for View bills and trust requests.

  • Approve bills and trust requests: Allow users to approve bills and trust requests that have been submitted for approval.

    Note: Enabling this permission will also enable View bills and trust requests.

  • Process bills and trust requests: Allow users to void bills and trust requests, and record payments.

    Note: Enabling this permission will also enable the View bills and trust requests and View bank accounts permissions.

  • Send bills and trust requests: Allow users to send bills and trust requests to clients, and mark bills as sent.

    Note: Enabling this permission will also enable the View bills and trust requests permission.

  • Create bills and trust requests: Allow users to create new bills, new trust requests, statements of accounts, legal aid bills, quick bills, and duplicate new requests.

    Note: Enabling this permission will also enable the View activities and View bills and trust requests permissions.

 

Firm settings

Firm settings permissions control a user's ability to view and manage your firm's administrative information. These permissions define what a user can do with firm-wide settings.

  • View account firm feed: Allow users to view the firm feed via the firm's dashboard.
  • Manage roles: Allow users to create, edit, archive, assign, and unassign roles to other firm users.
  • Manage users: Allow users to invite, remove, and edit firm user information.
  • Manage custom fields: Allow users to create, edit, delete, and convert contact and matter custom fields.
  • Manage location for review requests: Allow users to manage the Google business profile selected for Client Reviews.

 

Conflict check

Conflict check settings control a user's ability to initiate conflict checks and view the conflict check report. Learn about conflict checks.

  • Manage conflict checks: Any potential conflict found that is associated with a matter to which a user does not have access will appear as a line item marked as hidden and will be inaccessible to the user.

  • View conflict check report: By default, only administrators have the ability to view a conflict check report.

    Important: When applying this permission, a user will be able to view the full PDF report. The report includes information about all conflict check results, including details that the user may not normally have access to, as specified by the matter permissions.

 

Up next

  • Create and Manage Custom Roles: Build a custom role, apply the permissions described above, and edit or delete roles as your firm's needs change.
  • Assign and Unassign Roles: Once your custom roles are set up, assign them to users in your firm.
  • Roles and Permissions in Clio Manage: If you would rather use Clio's predefined roles instead of building your own, read this article for an overview of the roles available and the access each one provides.

results.name: Manage Tasks in Clio Manage
results.title: Manage Tasks in Clio Manage
results.body:
Tasks are an essential part of tracking matter-related activities and events in Clio Manage. You can create and edit tasks, track time against them, mark them as complete, and get an overview of upcoming deadlines.

Tip: You can use task types and task lists to efficiently manage similar tasks across multiple matters.

Task access and permissions

All firm users have access to the Tasks tab in Clio Manage and can view or edit their own tasks as well as tasks created by other users.

While there are no specific permissions available for tasks, you can set a task as private when creating or editing it. Setting a task to private makes it visible only to the task creator, the task assignee, and firm users with administrator permissions.

 

Create new tasks

When you create a task, it will appear in the matter timeline (if a matter is selected), on the Calendar on its due date, and in the Dashboard Firm Feed. Tasks can be created from the main Tasks tab or the Tasks subtab within a matter. All fields are optional except for the task name and the task assignee.

Note: Private tasks will not appear in the matter timeline or Firm Feed.

  1. Go to the main Tasks tab or the Tasks subtab within a matter.
  2. Click New Task.

  3. Complete the task details. Learn more about task types, assigning tasks, reminders and notifications, and task status.

    • Email notification: Internal firm members will only receive an email notification for the assigned task if the Notify assignee when task is assigned checkbox is checked.
    Tip: Use text formatting (like bold or italics) or lists to emphasize critical details. You can also add links to the description to reference other information, both inside and outside of Clio Manage. To link to other Clio Manage pages, right-click (Windows) or Control + Click (Mac OS) on the link you want to reference, select Copy Link Address, and then paste the link into the description.
  4. Click Save task to save this task and close the modal. Click Save and create another to save the task and open a new blank modal to create a new task. Click Save and duplicate to save the task and copy the details, reminders, and assignments.

 

Duplicate tasks

All firm users can duplicate tasks from the main Tasks tab or the Tasks subtab within a matter, or while editing a task. Duplicating tasks allows you to quickly create new tasks with the same details, reminders, and assignments. This helps maintain consistency and focus on the work itself.

Note: You can set tasks to repeat in Clio Manage by duplicating them to maintain consistency and efficiency across your matters.
Main tasks tab Matter subtab Edit task
  1. Go to Tasks.
  2. Find the task you want to duplicate.
  3. Click the dropdown arrow next to Mark complete and select Duplicate.
  4. Make any necessary changes.
  5. Click Save task.
  1. Go to the matter and click the Tasks subtab.
  2. Find the task you want to duplicate.
  3. Click the dropdown arrow next to Mark complete and select Duplicate.
  4. Make any necessary changes.
  5. Click Save task.
  1. Go to the main or matter Tasks tab.
  2. Click the dropdown arrow next to Mark complete and select Edit.
  3. Click Duplicate and make any necessary changes.
  4. Click Save task.

 

Edit tasks

You can edit an existing task in the main Tasks tab or the Tasks subtab within a matter. When you edit a task’s due date, you will no longer see the original due date. If you need to keep track of the original due date, make a note in the Description field.

  1. Go to the main Tasks tab or the Tasks subtab within a matter.
  2. For the relevant task, click the dropdown arrow in the Actions column and select Edit task.
  3. Make your changes.
  4. Click Save task.

Note: You can also edit a task in the Calendar.

 

Reassign tasks

There are several ways that you can reassign tasks.

  • You can reassign a single task when you edit the task by choosing a different individual or individuals in the Assign to field.
  • You can also reassign all tasks from a specific user to another. One scenario where this option may be useful is if you deactivate a user or if a user's work responsibilities change.
  • Finally, you can reassign a tasks or tasks from the main Task tab or from a matter's Tasks subtab to a user of your choosing. Follow the instructions below for this option.

Note: You can only bulk reassign tasks associated with open or pending matters.

To reassign a task or tasks

  1. Go to Tasks, or open a matter and go to the Tasks subtab.

  2. Use the checkbox(es) to select the task(s) you want to reassign.

    Tip: To select all tasks visible on the page, select the checkbox in the table header. You can also apply filters to narrow your list of tasks.
  3. Click Reassign.
  4. Under Assign to, select the firm member(s) or contact(s) added in Clio Manage you want to reassign the tasks to.
    • You can select up to ten individuals from either the firm members or from other contacts in Clio Manage. Select the Firm member or External radio buttons to switch between the two.
  5. Click Save.

 

Select task relative due date

When editing a task’s due date, you can select a specific date from the Calendar or select a relative due date that is based on an existing task for a matter. This means that the task will be due a specific amount of time before or after an existing task that is linked to the matter. When you update the due date for the first task, the task with the relative due date will automatically update to the same amount of time before or after the first task is due.

  1. Go to the main Tasks tab or the Tasks subtab within a matter.
  2. Find the task.
  3. Click the dropdown arrow next to Mark complete and select Edit task.
  4. Under Due date select Relative due date. Specify how long before or after another task this task should be due.
  5. Click Save task.

 

Update task due dates in bulk

Task due dates can be updated for individual tasks and for multiple tasks in bulk. When you bulk update task due dates for outstanding tasks, you can select an unlimited number of tasks. The tasks will all update to the same new due date.

Important: Tasks with relevant due dates will adjust according to the parameters specified in the relevant due date only if one of the tasks in the relevant connection is updated. If you bulk update two or more tasks that are connected via relevant due dates, they will have the same new due date, which means that the relevant due date connection will be broken.

  1. Go to the main Tasks tab or the Tasks subtab within a matter.
  2. Check the box next to multiple tasks.
  3. Click Edit date.
  4. Specify a new due date for all the tasks you selected.
  5. Click Save.

 

Add time to tasks

When tracking tasks for a matter, you can also add billable or non-billable time to the task. This ensures that your time is captured for any work in progress that may appear on a generated invoice.

  1. Go to the main Tasks tab or the Tasks subtab within a matter.
  2. Under the Recorded time column, click Add time.
  3. Complete the time entry and click Save entry.

 

Mark tasks complete or incomplete

When you mark a task as complete, the task moves to the Completed section of the Tasks table. Similarly, when you mark a completed task as incomplete, it moves to the Outstanding section of the table. You can perform these actions on individual tasks or in bulk. You can also view completed tasks in the matter Timeline and Firm Feed.

Note: You will not receive a notification if you complete one of your own tasks or if a task is overdue.

Mark complete or incomplete

You can mark tasks complete or incomplete, either individually or in bulk. 

Complete/incomplete single task Complete/incomplete multiple tasks
  1. Go to the main Tasks tab or the Tasks subtab within a matter.
  2. Click Mark complete. You can move the task back to incomplete by selecting the Completed tab and then clicking Mark incomplete.

Note: You can also mark a single task as complete in the Calendar.

  1. Go to the main Tasks tab or the Tasks subtab within a matter.
  2. Select the boxes next to the tasks or select the box in the table header to automatically check all tasks.
  3. Click Mark complete. Move the task back by clicking the Completed tab, checking boxes, and then clicking Mark incomplete.

View completed tasks

When a task is completed, you can view the completed task in either the Matter Timeline or in the Dashboard Firm Feed.

Via matter Timeline Via Firm Feed
  1. Go to the matter's Dashboard.
  2. Scroll down to Timeline.
  3. Click Filters and select Task under Type.
  4. Click Apply filters.
  1. Go to Dashboard > Firm Feed.
  2. Click Filter and select Task under Type.

 

Delete tasks

Important: Deleting tasks is a permanent action.

Any user can delete individual tasks that they have visibility on. Administrators and Primary Subscribers can delete tasks in bulk.

Delete single task Delete tasks in bulk
  1. Go to the main Tasks tab or the Tasks subtab within a matter.
  2. Click the down arrow next to Mark complete and select Delete task.
  3. When the warning prompt appears, select Delete.

Note: You can also delete a task in the Calendar.

  1. Go to the main Tasks tab or the Tasks subtab within a matter.
  2. Select the boxes next to the tasks or select the box in the table header to automatically check all tasks, and then select Delete.
  3. When the warning prompt appears, select Delete.

The Reputation Management dashboard in Clio Grow gives you a single place to track the review requests your firm sends to clients. Once you start sending review requests, you can use the dashboard to see important metrics about your review requests.

The top of your dashboard displays the most important metrics.

Total reviews requested

The total number of review requests your firm has sent to clients, including both manual and automatic requests.

results.name: Time Entries
results.title: Time Entries
results.body:
Time entries are one of two types of billable or non-billable activities that form a bill. Expenses are the other type of activity. Time entries can be created separately from other Clio Manage events, but you can also add time to other events in Clio Manage, such as documents, calendar events, tasks, and communications. Just click Add time beside each line item.

Tip: Track performance metrics for billable time for yourself or your entire firm using the personal and firm dashboards.

Add new time and flat rate entries

You can create a new time entry or flat rate entry from several places within Clio, making it a convenient way to keep on top of your time and expenses throughout the day. It can be done in the main Activities page in Clio Manage, the Activities page within a matter, and from the global Create new button on the top right of your Clio Manage screen.

  1. You can access the modal to add a new time or fixed rate entry from various locations in Clio Manage:
    • Go to Activities, then click New time entry, or
    • from the Clio Manage header, click Create new, or
    • from a matter’s Dashboard subtab, click Add time.
  2. Once in the modal, you can add the time or select an activity category, along with other details. Depending on how you navigated to the modal, some of the information may already be entered.
    • The Duration field allows for a number of different formats for entering time (e.g., 1h 12m, 1:12, 72min, and 1.2h). Note that the duration you enter here may be adjusted according to your firm's time rounding settings.
    • The Date field will usually be prefilled with the current date, or the date of the filter if creating from the Activities page. You can select any past, current, or future date.
    • For the Rate field, make you understand the Rate and Rate Hierarchies when entering details to understand which rate and currency will be used to calculate the time entry amount. Also note in particular the hierarchical position of the activity category in relation to the rates.
      If the client or matter’s preferred billing currency is different from the firm’s default currency, the Rate field’s currency will be the one you chose for recording time entries when you added the currency in Billing Settings.
    • Optional: If you have grants enabled, you can choose a relevant grant to associate with the time entry.
    • Optional: If your matter has LEDES billing enabled, select the relevant codes for the Activity category and UTBMS task code fields. These fields are required for LEDES-enabled matters unless the entry is marked as non-billable.
    • Optional: If you want to track non-billable time, check the Non-billable check box. When you do so, you can also choose whether to include the non-billable entry on a bill by checking Show this entry on the bill.
  3. Click Save entry to save the entry and exit the modal. Alternatively, click Save and > Ceate another to save the entry and open a new time entry modal. Click Save and > Duplicate to save the time entry and create a new entry with the same information pre-populated.

Tip: You can use AI features that can help you proactively identify matter activity and suggest unlogged time entries on AI Action Cards. You can also learn how to transforms your billing workflow using automated processes.

 

Play and pause timer

You can use the timer in Clio Manage to easily and accurately capture time for time entries. The timer can be started from anywhere in Clio Manage, making it a convenient and efficient way to stay on top of your activities. Click the clock beside the timer in the Clio Manage header to open the timekeeper. The timekeeper displays all time entries created that day. You can restart timers, edit entries, or create new time entries from one place and cycle through previous days using the arrows next to the date.

Note: You can also start the timer by opening a new time entry and clicking the play button. If you go to any unbilled time entry in the Activities tab and click the play button, this will start the timer for that entry, allowing you to add more time.

Tip: To confirm the exact time the timer was started, go to the Firm Feed in the Dashboard. Locate the entry that says [user name] created Time Entry, about [time] ago. The timestamp on the right will display the exact date and time the timer began.
  1. Click the play button in the Clio Manage header.
  2. Click the pause button to stop the time. A new time entry modal will open where you can save your time entry.

 

Create non-billable time entries

By default, time entries marked as non-billable will not appear on a generated bill because they are set to $0. If you need to show a non-billable time entry on a bill, you can do so easily when creating the time entry. By showing non-billable time on a bill, you can bill more accurately for non-billable activities, report on non-billable time, and show your clients extra value invested in their case.

Important: If you mark an activity as non-billable and choose to show it on the bill, it can only be shown when generating the bill using bulk billing. The activity will not show on the bill invoice if you generate a Quick bill.

  1. Create a new time entry or edit an existing time entry.
  2. Check the box for Non-billable to not charge for the time entry.
    • When a time entry is marked as non-billable, the Discount box is greyed out and set to 0%. You can still choose to show or not show the entry on the bill.
  3. Check the box for Show this entry on the bill to show the time entry on the bill at a $0 rate.

Change contingency fee and flat rate non-billable time

You can also change this setting and choose to set time entries for these matters to billable time. Once changed, the hourly time entries for these matters will automatically have a $0.00 rate that you can update manually. Follow the steps below to change the default behaviour.

Tip: Learn more about the contingency fee and flat rate matters workflow here.
  1. Go to Settings > Billing > General.

Duplicate time entries

Note: If an activity has been generated on a bill, the duplicate button will appear next to the time entry.
  1. Go to Activities and find the time entry you want to duplicate.

  3. Make any necessary changes and then select Save entry.

 

Edit time entries

You can edit an unbilled time entry from the main Activities page in Clio Manage or from the Activities subtab within a matter. All users can edit time entries, but only users with the applicable permissions to edit activities in bulk can do so.

Important: The edits you make will affect all selected time entries. The original time entry details will not be saved anywhere in Clio. Additionally, the matter field will be blocked if the selected time entries are from different matters.
Edit single time entry Edit time entries in bulk

Delete time entries

You can track deleted time entries in the Recovery bin, from a matter’s timeline, and from the Firm Feed. Deleted items will remain in the Recovery Bin for six months in case they need to be re-added and billed to clients. It is possible to recover deleted items, but Clio does not guarantee that the lost data can be recovered. The best practice is to ensure the item is not needed before deleting it, with the recovery bin available as a failsafe.

Delete one time entry Delete in bulk Recover deleted activity

results.title: Reports Permissions and Settings
results.body:
Access to reports in both Clio Grow and Clio Manage requires specific permissions on your user profile. Clio Manage users require reports permissions, and Clio Grow users require admin permissions to view reports. Additionally, Clio Manage administrators can change the payment allocation setting to determine how partial payments should be applied to certain reports.

Note: Only administrators can perform the actions listed in this article.

Change reports permissions in Clio Grow

In Clio Grow, a user can either have admin or normal permissions. Only users with admin permissions can view reports and provide access to other users to view reports. If you are an administrator, follow the steps below to give another firm user reports permissions.

Important: All users with admin permissions can view reports, export contacts and matters to CSV, invite users, deactivate users, add or remove licenses, and update firm billing information.
  1. Go to Settings > Account.
  2. In the User settings section, select a user’s Normal permission.
  3. Select Admin and then click Assign permission.

 

Change reports permissions in Clio Manage

In Clio Manage, users need reports permissions to view and generate reports. Once a user has reports permissions, they can view all reports in Clio Manage. You cannot restrict reports. If you are an administrator, follow the steps below to give another firm user report permissions.

Important: Granting a user reports permissions will give them access to other firm users’ productivity, including activities and billing rates, when viewing reports even if the user does not have billing permissions.
For one user For multiple users in bulk
  1. Go to Settings > Manage Users.
  2. Click Edit below the user’s name.
  3. Scroll down to Permissions.
  4. Check the box for Reports.
  5. Click Save New Information.
  1. Go to Settings > Groups, Permissions, and Job Titles > Permissions.
  2. Scroll down to Reports.
  3. Check or uncheck the boxes next to users’ names.

 

Change reports allocation setting in Clio Manage

Clio Manage reports help you quickly gauge how much of your client payments come from different line item categories. By default, partial payments and credit notes are applied to all line items proportionally. Administrators can also choose a different payment allocation method for how partial payments and credit notes are applied to line items in specific reports. Once a new method is selected, only reports generated after choosing the new method will be affected.

Note: This setting will affect the following reports: invoice payments report, fee allocation report, revenue report, and the originating attorney revenue report. This setting will also affect the collection rate in your Firm Dashboard.

  1. Go to Settings > Billing.
  2. Select Reports allocation.
  3. Under Payment allocation, select the allocation method of your choice. There are four allocation methods to choose from. See below for an explanation of each and a table with examples of how a partial payment would be allocated across report line items depending on the selected method.
    • Option 1: Pay all line items proportionally
    • Option 2: Pay expenses oldest to newest first and then services oldest to newest
    • Option 3: Pay expenses oldest to newest first and then services proportionally
    • Option 4: Pay services oldest to newest first and then expenses oldest to newest
  4. Click Save setting.

 

Allocation method explanation:

Option 1: Pay all line items proportionally

  • This is the default setting. A partial payment will be applied to line items based on each line item's percentage of the total bill cost. For example, a $400 expense on a $1000 invoice is 40% of the invoice. If that invoice receives a payment of $800, 40% of that partial payment amount is $320, so the expense will receive a $320 payment.
  • This method is also used by accounting systems like QuickBooks Online (QBO) and Xero. Use this method if you want your firm's reporting data in Clio Manage to match the reporting data in QBO or Xero. 

Option 2: Pay expenses oldest to newest first and then services oldest to newest

  • A partial payment will be first applied to expense line items from the oldest dated to newest dated, followed by services (time entries) from oldest dated to newest. If the payment is fully used before all line items are paid, the remaining line items will show $0 in reports.
  • If you use reports to determine how to pay employees based on their recorded time, you may want to use the option 3 (pay expenses oldest to newest first and then services proportionally) since option 2 will result in employees who did work earlier on the invoice being compensated first.

Option 3: Pay expenses oldest to newest first and then services proportionally

  • A partial payment will be first applied to expense line items from the oldest dated to newest dated. Services (time entries) will then be paid proportionally based on each service's percentage of the total of all services on the invoice, NOT the invoice total. This method can help pay all employees who did work on the invoice equally.
  • For example, if, after paying all expenses, there is $100 of a partial payment remaining and a total of $300 in services, with service 1 for $200 (two-thirds of the total service amount) and service 2 for $100 (one-third of the total service amount), service 1 will receive $66.67 and service 2 will receive $33.33. 

Option 4: Pay services oldest to newest first and then expenses oldest to newest

  • If you select this option, a partial payment will be first applied to service line items from the oldest dated to newest dated, followed by expense line items from oldest dated to newest. If the payment is fully used before all line items are paid, the remaining line items will show $0 in reports.

 

Example:

In this example, you sent your client a $1000 invoice with two expense line items and two service line items. Your client paid a partial payment of $800 toward the invoice. When you generate a report containing invoice line items, the four line items will be allocated the paid $800 depending on the allocation setting you chose. The table below shows how much of the payment would go toward each line item depending on each allocation method option.

 

Set allocations in Clio Manage

The fee allocation report is designed give your firm a detailed view of the time and expenses each user has billed and collected for each matter. To help you easily determine your firm's compensation and bonus structures, administrators can also set how much of the collected time in the fee allocation report should be allocated to originating attorney, responsible attorneys, and responsible staff. Previously generated reports will not be affected by updated attorney allocations.

Note: This is a firm-wide setting that will affect all fee allocation reports. Firm administrators can also override the firm-wide setting for any individual matter by changing the allocation percentages for that matter.

  1. Go to Settings > Billing.
  2. Select Reports allocation.
  3. Under Fee allocation, enter percentage allocations for the different firm members.
  4. Click Save setting.
