results.title: Legal Aid US: Grants Dashboards, Exports, and Reports
results.body:
View dashboards and metrics 

There are three different dashboards and an organization timeline to help you keep track of how time is spent on matters and grants:

Personal Dashboard:

This dashboard shows a high-level overview of your agenda, how you are spending your time, and financial metrics. A comprehensive description of the dashboard is provided here. When grant information is tracked it also includes information about how you are spending your time in relation to grants and their associated matters.

  • Time allocation: This section shows your time entries in hours for the specified timeframe. If grants are associated with any time entries, they are listed in this section.
    • You can use the Filter to display information about the proportion of time allocated to each grant in hours, as a percentage, or both.
    • You can click Review activities for any listed grant to view a table of the transactions associated with that grant.
    • You can select a date range and relevant filters to view specific information and export the data using Export CSV.

Organization Dashboard:

Note: The primary subscriber or users with administrator permissions can view this dashboard.

This dashboard shows a high-level overview of how firm members are spending their time and what their billing practices are. A comprehensive description of the dashboard is provided here. When grant information is tracked, it also includes information about how firm members are spending their time in relation to grants and on matters associated with grants.

  • Time allocation: This section shows time entries for the specified timeframe across firm users.
    • You can use the Filter to display information about the proportion of time allocated to each grant in hours, as a percentage, or both.
    • You can click Review activities for any listed grant to view a table of the transactions associated with that grant.
    • You can select a date range and relevant filters to view specific information and export the data using Export CSV.

Organization Feed:

This feed shows a timeline of all organization-wide activity in the account. A comprehensive description of the feed is provided here. Relevant to grants, the feed provides information related to grant spend down via salaries, such as updates to grant allocations, changes to salary amounts, and the spend down amounts.

Matter Dashboard:

This dashboard provides an overview of matter information. A comprehensive description of the feed is provided here. When you add a grant to a matter, that matter's dashboard will show a new section for grants associated with the matter.

 

Generate a matters and grants report

If you use grants at your firm, you can generate a Matters & grants report which offers information similar to a matter report but with additional options to filter by grant, matter custom fields, and client custom fields.

  1. Go to Reports.
  2. In the list of categories, select Matters.
  3. Click Matters & grants.
  4. Make your selections.
  5. Click Generate report.

 

Export matters with associated grants

In the main Matters tab, you can select columns and specify filters relevant to a particular export you may need to track a specific deliverable, including cases closed under a specific grant. When adding a grant to a matter, if you check the box for Use this grant for case reporting, the grant will appear in the Grants column and in the export.

Tip: When selecting your filters and columns, you also have the option to select custom fields. These custom fields will appear in your export, allowing you to report on them.

  1. Go to Matters.
  2. Click Columns, check the box for Grants, and then click Update columns.
  3. Select Filters to sort data by specific filters, including specific grants or custom fields, and then click Apply filters.
  4. Optional: In the search box, use a keyword search to filter your matters.
  5. Scroll to the bottom of the table and click Export.

 

Export activities with associated grants

In the main Activities tab, you can select columns and specify filters relevant to a particular export you may need to track a specific deliverable. To export grant information from the Activities tab:

  1. Go to Activities.
  2. Click Columns, check the boxes for Grant and Matter, and then click Update columns.
  3. Select Filters to sort data by specific filters, including specific grants, and then click Apply filters.
  4. Scroll to the bottom of the table and click Export.

 

Export grants

In the Grants tab, you can export your organization's grants to get an understanding of how much of a spend down there has been from the grants. The data will be exported in CSV format.

  1. Go to Grants.
  2. Scroll to the bottom of the table and click Export.
Note: All active and archived grants will be exported regardless of the subtab you selected.

 

Export grant transactions

You can export the transactions associated with a grant to get an understanding of the detailed financials of a specific grant. The data will be exported in CSV format and will show grant spend down in your firm.

  1. Go to Grants.
  2. Select the name of a grant to view its transactions.

  3. Optional: You can add or remove columns to include or exclude in the export by clicking Columns, selecting and/or deselecting column fields, and clicking Update columns.

    Note: You can select a time period to filter the list of transactions in the table, but the export will include all transactions for a grant regardless of the time period you selected.
  4. Scroll to the bottom of the table and click Export.
  5. Choose between exporting Available columns, which will include all available columns even if you previously deselected them, or Visible columns only to include only those columns you appearing in the table view.
  6. Click Export.

results.name: Court Rules
results.title: Court Rules
results.body:
With court rules, you can track court deadlines for your matters by selecting court trigger events for specific court jurisdictions. Once you select a trigger, court rules will automatically find related court events for the specified jurisdiction and add dates to your calendar.

Court rules provide automated rules-based calendaring from a library of court rules across 50 U.S. states and 2,200 jurisdictions. In Canada, court rules are available across two provincial courts and the federal court, with more provincial and territorial jurisdictions to be added in the future. In the UK and Australia, court rules currently support a limited set of conveyancing (property transaction) rule sets.

Add jurisdictions and configure settings

To get started with court rules, you need to select the relevant jurisdictions and configure your default settings in Clio Manage. Only administrators have permission to do this. After adding jurisdictions, you can configure your default settings for creating court rules calendar entries, including default jurisdiction, default service type, default calendar, and default attendees. Once created, court rules will appear on the calendar that you specified, and they will include your selected attendees.

Note: This feature is available to select plans. Learn more about your plan's features. Adding jurisdictions beyond what your plan provides are subject to an additional charge. If you need to upgrade your firm’s plan, ask a firm administrator.
Add jurisdictions Delete jurisdictions Configure default settings
  1. Go to Settings > Court Rules > Jurisdictions.
  2. Click Add new jurisdictions (if this is the first time adding jurisdictions) or Add jurisdictions (if you already have selected jurisdictions and want to add more).
  3. In the search field, start typing the name of the jurisdiction or court you want to add.
  4. From the list of options that appear, use the checkboxes to select all jurisdictions you want to add.

  5. Optional: Click the eye (view) icon next to the jurisdiction’s name to view the ruleset.

    Note: You can use the search field to search for additional jurisdictions. Any jurisdictions already selected will remain selected in the background until you’re ready to confirm your selections.

  6. When you’ve selected all jurisdictions you need, click Add jurisdictions.

    Note: If you selected more jurisdictions than allowed by your plan, you will be informed and will have to acknowledge the additional cost by clicking Confirm and add.

  1. Go to Settings > Court Rules > Jurisdictions.
  2. Click Add jurisdictions.
  3. Click the X next to a jurisdiction’s name to remove it.
  4. Read the message that explains the effects of removing a jurisdiction and click Confirm and remove to delete the jurisdiction.

Note: The default jurisdiction will automatically appear when you add a new rule to a matter and is selected from your list of jurisdictions. You can always change the default jurisdiction when adding a new rule to a matter. The default service type will only appear for triggers that require service delivery.

  1. Go to Settings > Court Rules > Default Settings.
  2. Select from the dropdown selections for Default Jurisdiction, Default Service Type, and Default Calendar.
  3. Search for firm users under Default Attendees.
  4. Click Update Court Rules Settings.

 

Add court rules to matters

In Clio Manage, you can add court rules to matters from either the main Calendar tab or a matter’s Calendar subtab. Once created, you can view the court rule and its associated calendar events in either location.

When creating a court rule, you can only select the trigger’s date and time. You cannot edit dates and times for any associated calendar events unless you edit that specific associated calendar event. Learn more about editing associated calendar events below.

Note: If a court deadline falls on a weekend or holiday, the event will be added to your calendar either the Friday before the weekend or holiday or the Monday after the weekend or holiday. Weekend and holiday deadlines vary by jurisdiction.

Tip:Some of your court rules associated events may contain the acronyms L/D or F/D. L/D means Last Day served, and F/D means First Day served.

Via Calendar tab Via Calendar subtab in matter
  1. Go to Calendar.
  2. Select the down arrow next to New event and select New court rule.
  3. In the Set Up section, complete the required fields. You can also enter details for the optional fields:
    • Required: the court rule's Name, the Matter, a previously added Jurisdiction, the court Trigger, and the trigger's Date.
    • Optional: the trigger's Time. The trigger’s start time will be shown in a one-hour block in your calendar, if applicable. You can create a longer or shorter time block after creating and saving the event.
    • Optional: a custom Event prefix. The custom prefix will be applied to ALL calendar events for this court rule. Additionally, the prefix can be both alphabetical text and numbers, will appear in email notifications and any synced calendars, and can only be edited one event at a time once applied.
  4. Optional: Select the Service Type. You will only see this field for some triggers, such as process serving.
  5. Click Next: Select Events.
  6. In the Select Events section, deselect any parent events that you do not want to be created as calendar entries. All events associated with the trigger are selected by default.
  7. Click Next: Choose Calendar Options.
  8. Select the calendar that the events will appear on and add firm user attendees. You can set reminders for the attendees now or later when editing the event.
  9. Click Add to Calendar.
  1. Go to the matter and click Calendar.
  2. Select the down arrow next to New event and select New court rule.
  3. In the Set Up section, complete the required fields. You can also enter details for the optional fields:
    • Required: the court rule's Name, a previously added Jurisdiction, the court Trigger, and the trigger's Date.
    • Optional: the trigger's Time. The trigger’s start time will be shown in a one-hour block in your calendar, if applicable. You can create a longer or shorter time block after creating and saving the event.
    • Optional: a custom Event prefix. The custom prefix will be applied to ALL calendar events for this court rule. Additionally, the prefix can be both alphabetical text and numbers, will appear in email notifications and any synced calendars, and can only be edited one event at a time once applied.
  4. Optional: Select the Service Type. You will only see this field for some triggers, such as process serving.
  5. Click Next: Select Events.
  6. In the Select Events section, deselect any parent events that you do not want to be created as calendar entries. All events associated with the trigger are selected by default.
  7. Click Next: Choose Calendar Options.
  8. Select the calendar that the events will appear on and add firm user attendees. You can set reminders for the attendees now or later when editing the event.
  9. Click Add to Calendar.

 

Edit court rules and events

If you created a court rule or if you have permission to edit a court rule on another user’s calendar, you can update the court rule’s trigger date and time, add reminders, add time, and bulk update any associated calendar events. You can make changes from the main Calendar tab or a matter’s Calendar subtab.

Tip: You can view which firm user made changes to a court rule or associated event in the Dashboard Firm Feed or from the matter’s Dashboard Timeline.
Note: If you see an error when editing a court rule, this means either (1) the court rule was generated before May 14, 2022, the date when the recalculate functionality was enabled in your Clio Manage account, or (2) the selected court jurisdiction has not been added to your account or is no longer available. Ask an administrator at your firm to check your jurisdiction settings.
Via Calendar tab Via Calendar subtab in matter
  1. Go to Calendar.
  2. Find the court rule event.
  3. Optional: Click Add time to create a time entry for the event.
  4. Click Edit event to edit the court rule event.
  5. Make changes to the court rule’s name and/or trigger date and time.
  6. Click Save changes.
  7. Scroll down to Event changes to select or deselect associated events that you want to update. You may see the following tags next to some events:
    • Court permission required: These events require permission from the court to alter a due date and are selected by default.
    • Custom date: These events were previously manually edited to change the date to a custom date and are deselected by default.
    • Repeating event: These events were created as a repeating event in the calendar and are selected by default to automatically update upon any changes to the trigger date.
  8. Click Save changes.

  1. Go to the matter’s Calendar subtab.
  2. Under Court rules, find the event and click Edit.
  3. Make changes to the court rule’s name and/or trigger date and time.
  4. Click Save changes.
  5. Scroll down to Event changes to select or deselect associated events that you want to update. You may see the following tags next to some events:
    • Court permission required: These events require permission from the court to alter a due date and are selected by default.
    • Custom date: These events were previously manually edited to change the date to a custom date and are deselected by default.
    • Repeating event: These events were created as a repeating event in the calendar and are selected by default to automatically update upon any changes to the trigger date.
  6. Click Save changes.

 

Edit only associated parent and child events

After creating a court rule, you can edit the date and time for any associated parent or child court events as long as the court rule was created on your calendar or as long as you have permission to edit another user’s calendar. Parent events are deadlines calculated directly from the trigger date. Child events are deadlines calculated from the date of a parent event. You can edit these events by dragging and dropping them to a new calendar date or by editing them directly in the Calendar or from the matter’s Calendar subtab.

Important: Some child events have their own dependent deadlines. After moving a child event, review the dates of those deadlines in the matter's Calendar subtab.

Tip: You can view which firm user made changes to a court rule or associated court event in the Dashboard Firm Feed or from the matter’s Dashboard Timeline.
Via Calendar tab Via Calendar subtab in matter Via drag and drop
  1. Go to Calendar.
  2. Find the associated event.
  3. Optional: Click Add time to add a time entry to the event.
  4. Click Edit event to edit the event.
  5. In the new window, make your changes.
  6. Click Save event.
  7. If your selected parent court event has child events, you can select which child events you also want to automatically update.
  8. Click Move related events to save your changes. Click Don’t move to save your changes to the parent event without moving any of the child events.

  1. Go to the matter’s Calendar subtab.
  2. Under Calendar events, find the event and click Edit.
  3. In the new window, make your changes.
  4. Click Save event.
  5. If your selected parent court event has child events, you can select which child events you also want to automatically update.
  6. Click Move related events to save your changes. Click Don’t move to save your changes to the parent event without moving any of the child events.

  1. Go to Calendar.
  2. Click and hold the event and then drag and drop it to a new calendar date.
  3. If your selected parent court event has child events, you can select which child events you also want to automatically update.
  4. Click Move related events to save your changes. Click Don’t move to save your changes to the first event without moving any of the related events.

 

Add reminders to events

You can add reminders to events that you created and to events that are made available to the entire firm. You can add reminders from the main Calendar tab or the matter’s Calendar subtab.

Via Calendar tab Via Calendar subtab in matter
  1. Go to Calendar.
  2. Select the event and click Edit event.
  3. Under Reminders, click Add new reminder.
  4. Add a firm user and amount of time before the event they should receive a reminder.
  5. Repeat steps 3 and 4 to add additional reminders.
  6. Under Save to this calendar, if you check the box for Add this event to the Firm calendar as well as the selected calendar, all firm users can add reminders for the event.
  7. Click Save event.
  1. Go to the matter’s Calendar subtab.
  2. Select the event and click Edit.
  3. Under Reminders, click Add new reminder.
  4. Add a firm user and amount of time before the event they should receive a reminder.
  5. Repeat steps 3 and 4 to add additional reminders.
  6. Under Save to this calendar, if you check the box for Add this event to the Firm calendar as well as the selected calendar, all firm users can add reminders for the event.
  7. Click Save event.

 

Delete court rules and events

You can delete a single court rule and all its subsequent associated events from the Calendar tab or the matter’s Calendar subtab.

Via Calendar tab Via Calendar subtab in matter
  1. Go to Calendar.
  2. Select the event and click Delete.
  3. When the warning prompt appears, select Delete event.
  1. Go to the matter’s Calendar subtab.
  2. Under Court rules, find the event and click Delete.
  3. When the warning prompt appears, select Delete court rule.

In Clio Manage, each matter has a dashboard that provides an overview of matter information, such as financials, work in progress, basic matter details, custom fields, a timeline of matter-related events, contacts linked to the matter, and related contacts for the matter. 

Tip: You can also add related or associated matters to a contact's dashboard in case you need to connect a matter to a contact that may not necessarily be a case for that contact. Learn more about associated matters here.

Access matter's dashboard

You can access a single matter's dashboard from a few places in Clio Manage.

Matters tab Contact's dashboard Search bar Recents
  1. Go to Matters.
  2. Find your matter and click the matter’s name.
  1. Go to Contacts or search for the contact in the search bar.
  2. Find your contact and click the contact's name.
  3. In the Client's matters section of the contact's Dashboard, click the matter's name.
  1. Click the search bar in the Clio Manage header.
  2. Search for your matter and click the matter's name.
  1. Click Recents in the Clio Manage header.
  2. If you recently viewed the matter, click the matter's name under Matters.

 

Manage matter dashboard sections

Financial/ Activities and Grants

This section shows key financial information, such as work in progress, outstanding bill balance, matter trust funds, matter budget, and time and expenses. In this section, you can create a quick bill, view bills for this matter, request matter trust funds, add time and expense entries, and manage payment methods. 

  • Manage payment methods: If your firm has Clio Payments enabled, you can add new payment methods for the matter, request payment methods from the client on the matter, and manage current payment methods. Learn more about requesting and storing payment methods here.
  • Work in progress: The value in this section shows the combined total of all unbilled time entries for this matter, including any time entires on bills in draft and bills pending approval (unbilled). From this section, you can click Quick bills to generate a quick bill.
  • Outstanding balance: The value in this section shows the total amount due on approved bills for this matter. Trust requests are not included in this total. Click View bills to view all outstanding bills for this matter. 
  • Matter trust funds: This section shows the total trust fund amount held at the matter-level for this matter, including the minimum trust fund balance. If the client has funds held at the client-level (in the same currency as the matter), this section will also display a link to View client level funds. If funds held at the client-level is in a currency that is different from the matter, this will not be displayed. Click New request to generate a new trust request or Edit to edit the minimum trust balance for the matter. Learn more about trust account management here and the minimum trust balance feature within the matter form here.

  • Budget: If a budget amount was set in the Billing Preferences of the matter, this section shows a progress bar with the value of current billed activities relative to the budget amount.

    Note: The budget calculations exclude tax amounts.

  • Time: This value shows the gross total for all time entries logged by your firm on this matter. Click Add time to add a new time entry. Learn more about time entries here.
  • Expenses: This value shows the gross total for all expense entries logged by your firm on this matter. Click Add expense to add a new expense entry. Learn more about expenses here.
  • Grants table: A table displays grant information for matters with Legal Aid.
Matter details

This section shows matter details that you entered when you first created the matter. You can change the information in these fields by editing the matter. You can update the matter status (to open, pending, or closed) from here.

eFiling

This section shows the status of documents that a firm user submitted electronically to your local courts using Clio's e-filing feature. You can manage draft filings in the matter's E-filing subtab and view completed submissions, including court-stamped documents in the Documents subtab. Learn more about e-filing here.

Custom fields

This section shows the custom fields that you added to the matter when you first created the matter. You can change these custom fields by editing the matter. Learn more about editing matters here and more about custom fields here.

Contacts

This section shows the clients and related contacts associated with the matter, their basic contact information, including phone number, email address, address, and tags added to the contact. From this section, you can also do the following:

  • Click on any contact name to navigate directly to the contact where you can then see additional details or update to the contact's information.
  • If the contact has a textable phone number and you have text messaging enabled for your account, click Text to start a text conversation with the contact.
  • Click the contact's phone number to open your preferred call service app (outside of Clio) to start a call with the contact.
  • Click the contact's email address to open your preferred email service (outside of Clio Manage) and start composing an email to them.
  • Click the copy icon to copy the contact's physical address to your clipboard.
  • Click Edit for a contact to modify the contact via the contact page. 

For related contacts you can also click Sort by to sort the list by name in ascending (A-Z) or descending (Z-A) order. After applying a sort, select List order to return the list to the default order.

Timeline

This section shows a timeline of all activity on the matter, including anything that was created, edited, or deleted. Click Filters to sort the timeline by user, type of matter activity, and/or whether an activity item was deleted.

Conflict checks

This section shows the conflict checks run for the matter. You can also click Link conflict check to link a check that should be associated with the matter or click Run conflict check to run a new check.

Docket updates

This section shows any docket updates from docket alerts set up for the matter.

Recent Vincent conversations

Users with Clio Work have access to this section in a matter's dashboard. This section lists the most recent Vincent conversations started on the matter, showing who started each one and when it was last updated. From this section, you can do the following:

  • Click a conversation name to open that conversation in Clio Work.
  • Click View all to see every Vincent conversation for the matter.
  • Click Open Clio Work to go to the matter's dedicated workspace in Clio Work, where you can select workflows and ask questions relevant to only that matter.

Learn more about conversations with your AI research assistant, Vincent.

AI Actions

Clio's AI features work in the background of each matter to make helpful suggestions about next steps to take for the matter, for example scheduling calendar events, creating notes, tasks, or expense entries, billing your client, drafting communications, and more. Learn more about Clio's AI features. If your firm also uses Clio Work, you may see suggestions about potential research questions to ask or matter documents to can analyze. Learn more about your AI research assistant, Vincent.

Catch up

Catch up is in Beta. Review the summary against the matter before relying on it for client work or deadlines.

Note: This feature is available to select plans. Learn more about your plan's features. If you need to upgrade your firm’s plan, ask a firm administrator.

If your firm has Clio's AI features enabled, this section shows an AI-generated summary of what has happened on the matter, so you can get up to speed without opening each tab. The summary covers recent activity such as documents, communications, and matter updates, and refreshes automatically. An indicator in the top-right corner of the widget shows whether the summary is current.

Give feedback: Click the thumbs up or thumbs down icon to tell Clio whether the summary was useful. Your feedback helps improve future summaries.

Tip: You can also ask for a matter summary on demand, or ask targeted questions about a matter's activity and financials using Clio's AI features.

 

Customize matter dashboard

In Clio Manage, you can customize which sections (widgets) appear on a matter's Dashboard tab and how they are arranged.

Every firm user can customize their own matter dashboard.

Important: Your layout is personal and applies to every matter you open. Rearranging, resizing, or removing a widget on one matter changes the dashboard for all of your matters. It does not change what anyone else at your firm sees, and other firm users cannot change your layout.
  1. Go to a matter's dashboard.
  2. Turn on the New dashboard toggle in the matter header.
  3. Click the customize icon beside the toggle. The customizing toolbar appears at the top of the dashboard.
  4. Make your changes:
    • To reorder widgets, drag a widget to a new position.
    • To resize a widget, drag its bottom-right corner.
    • To remove a widget, click the X in its top-right corner.
    • To add a widget back, click Add widget and select it from the list.
    • To undo all of your customizations and return to Clio's default layout, click Reset to default.
  5. Click Save to keep your changes.
Tip: You can also move a widget using the arrow keys on your keyboard, and leave customizing using the Esc key on your keyboard.

results.name: Record Manual Bill Payments
results.title: Record Manual Bill Payments
results.body:
You can record payments received outside Clio Payments, like cash, checks, wire transfers, or ACH payments, and edit or delete these payments, then track their history. Accurately recording manual bill payments helps keep a client's balance current and your firm's books reconciled. Complete records show what is paid, what is outstanding, and where every payment landed.

Note: If your client paid by credit card or eCheck through Clio Payments, see Record and Manage Online Bill Payments. To record a payment from client trust funds, see Apply Trust Funds to Bills. 

Understand manual payment sources

Direct payment:

Record a payment received outside Clio Payments, such as cash, check, wire transfer, or ACH.

Other:

Record payment from an external platform such as Cash App or Venmo or a credit card processed outside Clio Payments.

Trust account:

Apply trust funds already received at the client or matter level toward a bill.

 

Record a single bill or multi-matter bill payment

You record payment for a single bill and a multi-matter bill the same way. A multi-matter bill is one bill that includes activities for multiple matters belonging to one client.

Note: On a multi-matter bill, payment applies to the oldest created matter first.

  1. Go to the Billing tab, or the Bills subtab in a matter or contact.
  2. Select the Unpaid subtab.
  3. In the Actions column, next to Send, click the down arrow and select Record payment.
  4. Select one of the options for the Payment source, the deposit account, payer, and amount paid.
    • When the amount paid is less than the amount due, you can write off the remaining amount and add a description or note.
  5. If you use multiple currencies, and the client's payment currency differs from the bill or deposit account currency, the applicable conversion rate and any conversion loss or gain will be shown at the time of payment:
    • If the payment currency differs from the selected deposit account currency: Losses will be written off if the client paid the invoice amount(s) in full.
    • If the payment currency differs from the bill currency and results in an underpayment at the time of the deposit/payment: You can opt to write off the remaining amount.
    • If the payment currency differs from the bill currency and results in an overpayment at the time of the deposit/payment: The invoice will be considered paid in full.
  6. Click Record payment.

 

Record payment for one client's multiple bills

Note: You cannot record payments for bills belonging to different clients at the same time.

  1. In Clio Manage, click Billing.
  2. Click Record payment.
  3. Search for the client. All unpaid bills for that client appear.
  4. Select one of the options for the Payment source, the deposit account, payer, and amount paid. 
    • When the amount paid is less than the amount due, you can write off the remaining amount and add a description or note.
  5. If you use multiple currencies, and the client's payment currency differs from the bill or deposit account currency, the applicable conversion rate and any conversion loss or gain will be shown at the time of payment:
    • If the payment currency differs from the selected deposit account currency: Losses will be written off if the client paid the invoice amount(s) in full.
    • If the payment currency differs from the bill currency and results in an underpayment at the time of the deposit/payment: You can opt to write off the remaining amount.
    • If the payment currency differs from the bill currency and results in an overpayment at the time of the deposit/payment: The invoice will be considered paid in full.
  6. Click Record payment.

 

Record bill payments from trust funds

If your client has trust funds on the client or matter level, you can record payment for a bill from the trust funds. You can record payment and apply trust funds at the same time as the bill approval process or after a bill has already been approved. The bill moves to paid, or shows the remaining balance when trust funds do not cover the full amount.

When paying bills with client-level trust funds, Clio Manage generates three distinct transactions to accurately represent the movement of funds. These transactions record: a transfer to the matter balance (the system prevents edits to this transaction), a transfer from the client-level trust funds, and a transfer to your operating account to pay the invoice.

Note: If the trust funds are not sufficient to cover the total bill payment, the bill will remain in the Unpaid state with the remaining balance.

Note: If evergreen trust is enabled for the matter, applying trust funds to a bill can automatically generate a new replenishment trust request and clear the matter's existing trust request using the Clear old trust requests to prevent duplicates checkbox. Learn more about evergreen trust replenishment.

Apply trust to individual bills

Approve bill and apply trust funds Apply trust funds to approved bill
  1. Go to Billing or the Bills subtab in a matter or contact.
  2. Select either the Draft or Pending approval subtab.
  3. Click the down arrow next to Edit and select Approve & apply trust.
  4. Select your operating account as the destination account for payment.
  5. Click Approve & apply trust.
  1. Go to Billing or the Bills subtab in a matter or contact.
  2. Select the Unpaid subtab.
  3. Click the down arrow next to Send and select Record payment. You can also click Record payment in the upper right corner.
  4. If your client has trust funds, you will see a table showing the amounts on the matter and contact levels. From the Source dropdown, select your client’s trust funds.
  5. Complete the remaining details.
  6. Click Record payment.
Tip: For a quicker way to apply trust funds to a bill, in step 3, click the down arrow next to Send and select Apply trust funds. Then, select the destination account and click Apply trust.

 

Apply trust to multiple bills

You can also perform bulk actions to approve bills or to apply trust to approved bills

Approve bills and apply trust funds Apply trust funds to approved bills
  1. Go to Billing or the Bills subtab in a matter or contact.
  2. Select either the Draft or Pending approval subtab.
  3. Use the checkboxes to select relevant bills.
    • Make sure not to select any trust requests. If you accidentally do select a trust request, it will be excluded from the next action.
  4. Click the down arrow at the top of the table and select Approve & apply trust.
  5. Select your operating account as the destination account for payment.
  6. Click Approve & apply trust.
  1. Go to Billing or the Bills subtab in a matter or contact.
  2. Select the Unpaid subtab.
  3. Use the checkboxes to select relevant bills.
    • Make sure not to select any trust requests. If you accidentally do select a trust request, it will be excluded from the next action.
  4. Click the down arrow at the top of the table and select Apply trust.
    • A modal will appear with a summary list of the funds that will be applied to each bill. The summary list will only provide details of funds available to apply to the bills you selected. If you selected a bill, but no funds are available, no further action will occur for that bill.
  5. Select the destination account.
  6. Click Apply trust.

The Job status page will show you which bills were successfully approved and trust applied (Apply trust complete) and which bills were approved without applying trust (Approve invoice complete). The latter scenario occurs if no trust funds are available.

 

View bill payment history

After a payment is recorded, you can see which firm user recorded it in three places:

Bill Timeline:

Open a bill and, under Bill Timeline, view its creation and payment history.

Firm Feed:

Go to Dashboard > Firm Feed, click Filter, and under Type select Bill payment or Trust request payment.

Matter Timeline:

Open the matter Dashboard, scroll to Timeline, and filter by bill payment or trust request.

 

Up next

  • Edit and Delete Bill Payments: Change or remove a recorded bill payment.
  • Record Payments on Trust Requests: Record a client's trust deposit before you apply it to a bill.

Clio Grow offers a dashboard that can help you understand the performance of your marketing efforts. results.name: Navigate Contact's Dashboard
results.title: Navigate Contact's Dashboard
results.body:
In Clio Manage, you can open a dashboard for each contact that collects contact information, custom fields, billing information, the client's matters, and associated matters in one place. Company contacts also include employees, and contacts include Know Your Client (KYC) check history once your firm enables the KYC field set. The dashboard lets you check matters, billing, and history before you act on the file, and edit details, start a bill, or link a matter without searching for the contact again.

Tip: Each subtab across the top of the dashboard holds a different record type for the contact: Documents, Bills, Transactions, Communications, Notes, and Clio for Co-Counsel.

Open contacts dashboard

You can reach a contact dashboard from four places in Clio Manage. In each case, Dashboard is the first subtab for the contact you select.

From the contacts table

  1. In Clio Manage, click Contacts.
  2. Optional: Click Filters to narrow your contact results.
  3. Click the contact name.

 

From a matter dashboard

  1. In Clio Manage, click Matters.
  2. Optional: Click Filters to narrow your matter results.
  3. Click the matter name.
  4. In the Contacts section of the matter dashboard, click the contact name.

 

From the search bar

  1. In Clio Manage, click the search bar in the header.
  2. Enter the contact name, then click the relevant search result.

 

From Recents

  1. In Clio Manage, click Recents in the header.
  2. Under Contacts, click the contact name.

 

Understand dashboard sections

Each section on the dashboard reflects information entered when the contact was created or last edited. To change any of it, edit the contact.

Contact information

Holds the phone number, email address, website, and address for the contact. Click the email address to compose an email outside Clio Manage. Click the clipboard icon to copy the address. If your firm enables text messaging and the contact has a number you can text, click Text to start a text conversation.

Custom fields

Holds the contact custom fields added to the record. The dashboard displays the first 12 custom fields in the order they were added.

Billing information

Holds the LEDES client ID, payment profile, autocharge setting, rate table, rates, and default payment method for the contact. If your firm enables Clio Payments, click Manage to add a payment method, request a payment method from the client, or update a stored payment method.

Client's matters

Lists matters where this contact is the client. Click All for every matter or Open for open matters only. Click New matter to add a matter, or click Edit beside a matter name to change it. Click the down arrow beside Edit for Quick bill and Duplicate.

Associated matters

Lists matters where this contact holds a relationship but is not the client, such as a matter a co-counsel contact works on. The newest matters appear first.

Employees

Available on company contacts. Lists the person contacts linked to the company, along with the role recorded for each one. Click Add employee to link another person contact.

KYC check history

Available when your firm enables the Know Your Client (KYC) field set. Holds the KYC check information logged for the contact and for the contact's matters. Click Export to download the card as a CSV file.

 

Link associated matters to a contact

Link a matter to a contact when the contact holds a relationship to the matter without being the client on it. A linked matter appears in the Associated matters section of the contact dashboard and in the Related contacts section of the matter.

  1. In Clio Manage, click Contacts, then click the contact name.
  2. In the Associated matters section, click Link matter.
  3. Select the matter, then enter the relationship between the contact and the matter.
  4. Click Save.

 

Edit or remove a matter relationship

  1. In the Associated matters section, click the pencil icon beside the matter name.
  2. Update the relationship, then click Save. To end the link, click Delete, then click Delete relationship.

Note: Custom fields that use the contact select field type appear under the linked matter in the Associated matters section. For example, a spouse recorded as a contact select custom field on a matter appears beneath that matter in the list. To add or remove these custom fields, edit the matter.

 

Up next

  • Edit and Delete Contacts: Update the information held in the dashboard sections.
  • Add Employees to Company Contacts: Record the people who work at a company contact.

results.name: Get Started With Clio File
results.title: Get Started With Clio File
results.body:
Clio File is an all-in-one solution for e-filing and e-service. Built directly into Clio Manage and certified by the courts, Clio File allows you to e-file documents with your local courts and e-serve legal notice to parties right from a matter in Clio Manage. With Clio Manage's built-in e-filing solution, you have everything you need to e-file, e-serve, manage, and monitor your court filings, all from the same platform you use to run your law firm. Clio File can also use autofill to extract case and party details from your documents, so you only need to review the details before you submit.

Note: At this time, Clio File is only available in the following US states and counties.

Tip: You can learn how to initiate a filing and check filing statuses in File and Serve Documents and Track and Manage Filings. To set autofill or manual eFiling submission as your default, go to Settings, then eFiling, then Preferences, and select an option under Default eFiling method.

View available courts

You can use this section to confirm if Clio File is available for your business address and specific court location. Verifying jurisdictional support ensures your e-filings and e-services comply with local court requirements.

To use Clio File, you must have a verified business address in a supported state. You can view and update your address in your account settings.

California

Clio File is currently available in all California state courts that offer e-filing.

Note: Self-serve cancellation is not currently available for California filings. If you need to cancel a submission in this jurisdiction, please contact Clio Support immediately for assistance.

Georgia

You can use Clio File to e-file criminal, civil, and appellate documents in supported Georgia courts. Review the tables below to confirm county-specific support for Superior and State courts.

Note: You can cancel a filing submission directly in Clio File if the court has not yet processed the request. This allows you to correct errors or update documents without duplicate filing fees.

Georgia Superior Courts

 

Georgia State Courts

Use Clio File to e-file documents in the following Georgia State Courts.

Texas

In Texas, e-filing is required for all criminal and civil matters, as well as appeals supported at the District and County Court levels.

Note: Clio File supports direct cancellation for Texas filings. If you identify a mistake after submission, you can stop the filing process within the platform, provided the court status is still pending.

Illinois

Clio File is available in all Illinois courts that offer e-filing via the state's e-filing system.

Note: Clio File supports direct cancellation for Illinois filings. If you identify a mistake after submission, you can stop the filing process within the platform, provided the court status is still pending.

Nevada

Clio File is available in all Nevada courts that offer e-filing via the state's e-filing system.

Note: Clio File supports direct cancellation for Nevada filings. If you identify a mistake after submission, you can stop the filing process within the platform, provided the court status is still pending.

Virginia

Clio File is available to a limited number of counties in Virginia. Before filing, contact your court clerk to confirm whether Clio File is supported in your county.

Note: Clio File supports direct cancellation for Virginia filings. If you identify a mistake after submission, you can stop the filing process within the platform, provided the court status is still pending.

 

Sign up for Clio File

You can sign up for Clio File in your Clio Manage settings or from any matter's Dashboard. Once activated, you can add firm user filers and begin e-filing court documents and serving notice to parties directly from Clio Manage. 

Note: Only administrators can sign up for Clio File.

E-filings Settings Matter's Dashboard
  1. Go to the main eFiling tab.
  2. Click Activate today.
  3. Complete the required fields for your firm's information and check the box for the terms and conditions. 
  4. Click Activate.

  2. Click Activate today.
  3. Complete the required fields for your firm's information and check the box for the terms and conditions. 
  4. Click Activate.

  2. In the E-filing box, click Activate today.

  5. Click Activate.

 

Add and view firm user filers

Firm filers are users on your firm account who can e-file and serve court documents. You can designate any firm user on your account as a firm filer. Users not listed as firm filers can still initiate filings for any matter if an administrator has activated Clio File on the firm account and the user has the necessary permissions to access the matter. Once these users begin the filing process, they will automatically be added to the firm filer list.

Note: Only administrators can add firm user filers on the settings page and view the list of all firm filers.

  1. Go to Settings > E-filing.
  2. Check that you are viewing the E-filing account subtab.
  3. Click Add filer.
  4. Under Filer name, select a firm user.
  5. Optional: Under Bar number, enter the firm user's bar number.
  6. Click Save.

results.name: Calendar Events
results.title: Calendar Events
results.body:
In Clio Manage, you can create, edit, duplicate, and delete calendar events directly from the Calendar tab or from the Calendar subtab for a matter. When creating events, you can choose which calendar the event should appear on, add invite attendees and reminders, select calendar event types to distinguish events by color, and more. You can also share calendars for other users to view events.

Tip: Learn more about calendar sharing and permissions.

Create calendar events

Calendar events can be created from the Calendar subtab (where you do not need to select a matter), from a matter’s Calendar subtab, or from the global create new button. Calendar event attendees can be contacts or firm users. 

If a contact has an email address or phone number that you can text, the contact will receive a notification of the new event. Firm users will not receive notifications by default, but you can choose to send them email notifications. Events will also be visible in their calendars. You can also set up reminders for calendar events. Learn more about calendar notifications and reminders.

Note: The same calendar event’s time may be different on two separate calendars if the two users have different time zones. You can change your timezone in Settings > Profile.
Tip: You can view who created or edited a calendar event in the Dashboard Firm Feed.
Calendar tab Matter's Calendar subtab Create new button
Tip: If you double-click directly on a calendar date, the event creation window will automatically open for that date.
  1. Go to Calendar.
  2. Click New event.
  3. Complete the event details, such as title, start and end time, location of the event, description, and event type. Learn more about event types in the section below.
  4. Optional: If you previously connected your Zoom account with Clio, check the box for Make this a Zoom meeting to automatically add a Zoom meeting link once the event has been created. Learn more about Clio's integration with Zoom.
  5. Under Invite attendees, add contact and/or firm user attendees and choose how to notify them of the event.
    • The matter’s contact will appear as a suggested attendee under Suggested attendees. You can click the contact’s name to add them as an attendee.
    • Contact attendees will receive an email notification of the calendar event. Firm user attendees will not receive an email notification unless you choose to send one after saving the event.
    • You can also choose to send notifications via Clio for Co-Counsel for external counsel attendees or Clio for Clients for any client attendees who have an active client portal. Notifications sent via Clio for Co-Counsel and Clio for Clients will also be sent by email. Attendees who are notified by only email will have also be able to add the event to their personal calendars. Learn more about event notifications.
    • If the attendee has a valid North American phone number with texting enabled, check the box next to Notify via text to also notify the attendee of the event by text. Learn more about text messaging in Clio Manage.
  6. Optional: Add a reminder. Learn more about reminders.
  7. Under Save to this calendar, select which calendar to save the event to. You can only select a calendar that you created or that has been shared with you.
  8. Click Save event.
  1. Go to the matter and select the Calendar subtab.
  2. Click New event.
  3. Complete the event details, such as title, start and end time, location of the event, description, and event type. Learn more about event types in the section below.
  4. Optional: If you previously connected your Zoom account with Clio, check the box for Make this a Zoom meeting to automatically add a Zoom meeting link once the event has been created. Learn more about Clio's integration with Zoom.
  5. Under Invite attendees, add contact and/or firm user attendees and choose how to notify them of the event.
    • The matter’s contact will appear as a suggested attendee under Suggested attendees. You can click the contact’s name to add them as an attendee.
    • Contact attendees will receive an email notification of the calendar event. Firm user attendees will not receive an email notification unless you choose to send one after saving the event.
    • You can also choose to send notifications via Clio for Co-Counsel for external counsel attendees or Clio for Clients for any client attendees who have an active client portal. Notifications sent via Clio for Co-Counsel and Clio for Clients will also be sent by email. Attendees who are notified by only email will have also be able to add the event to their personal calendars. Learn more about event notifications.
    • If the attendee has a valid North American phone number with texting enabled, check the box next to Notify via text to also notify the attendee of the event by text. Learn more about text messaging in Clio Manage.
  6. Optional: Add a reminder. Learn more about reminders.
  7. Under Save to this calendar, select which calendar to save the event to. You can only select a calendar that you created or that has been shared with you.
  8. Click Save event.
  9. Optional: In the calendar events table, click Add time under the Recorded time column to create a time entry for the event.
    • If you do not see the option to add time, click Columns above the calendar events table and check that the Recorded time column is selected.
  1. Click Create new and select Event.
  2. Complete the event details, such as title, start and end time, location of the event, description, and event type. Learn more about event types in the section below.
  3. Optional: If you previously connected your Zoom account with Clio, check the box for Make this a Zoom meeting to automatically add a Zoom meeting link once the event has been created. Learn more about Clio's integration with Zoom.
  4. Under Invite attendees, add contact and/or firm user attendees and choose how to notify them of the event.
    • The matter’s contact will appear as a suggested attendee under Suggested attendees. You can click the contact’s name to add them as an attendee.
    • Contact attendees will receive an email notification of the calendar event. Firm user attendees will not receive an email notification unless you choose to send one after saving the event.
    • You can also choose to send notifications via Clio for Co-Counsel for external counsel attendees or Clio for Clients for any client attendees who have an active client portal. Notifications sent via Clio for Co-Counsel and Clio for Clients will also be sent by email. Attendees who are notified by only email will have also be able to add the event to their personal calendars. Learn more about event notifications.
    • If the attendee has a valid North American phone number with texting enabled, check the box next to Notify via text to also notify the attendee of the event by text. Learn more about text messaging in Clio Manage.
  5. Optional: Select a matter.
  6. Optional: Add a reminder. Learn more about reminders.
  7. Under Save to this calendar, select which calendar to save the event to. You can only select a calendar that you created or that has been shared with you.
  8. Click Save event.

 

Edit calendar events

You can edit a single calendar event from the Calendar subtab in a matter or from the main Calendar tab, where you can drag and drop events. In the month view, you can change the event's date by dragging and dropping it to a new spot. In the week view, you can change both the date and time of the event by dragging and dropping it to a new spot. Once an event is edited and saved, contact attendees will receive a notification of the change.

Important: You can only edit events from the calendar in which they were created. This means that if the event was created in the firm calendar and has been shared with you, you can only make changes from the firm calendar.
Calendar tab Matter's Calendar subtab
Tip: You can drag and drop calendar events to any other location in the calendar. If you are viewing your calendar using the month view, this action will only change the date, not the time of the event. If you are viewing your calendar using the week view, this action will change both the date and the time.
  1. Go to Calendar.
  2. Select the event on the calendar on which the event was created. You can see which calendar the event was created on when viewing the event modal.
  3. Click Edit event.
  4. Make your changes.
  5. Click Save event.
  1. Go to the matter and click Calendar.
  2. Optional: Click Filters to filter the events.
  3. Find the event and click Edit. You can see which calendar the event was created on below the Calendar column.
  4. Make your changes.
  5. Click Save event.

 

Duplicate calendar events

You can duplicate a single calendar event from the event preview, when editing an event, or from a matter's Calendar subtab. After clicking duplicate, the event details will open, allowing you to make any necessary changes before saving the event.

Tip: When you duplicate an event, it duplicates to your personal calendar.
Note: You can duplicate calendar events if you have view or edit access in Clio Manage. Recurring events, court rules, and private events imported from Outlook 365 or Google cannot be duplicated.
Event preview Matter subtab Edit event
  1. Go to Calendar.
  2. Select the event on the calendar where it was created. You can confirm the event's original calendar when viewing the event modal.
  3. Click the Clone icon in the top right corner of the event preview.
  4. Make any necessary changes.
  5. Click Save event.
  1. Go to the matter and click Calendar.
  2. Optional: Click Filters to filter the events.
  3. Find the event, click its dropdown arrow, and select Duplicate. You can confirm the event's original calendar below the Calendar column.
  4. Make any necessary changes.
  5. Click Save event.
  1. Go to the main or matter Calendar tab.
  2. Find the event and click Edit. You can confirm the event's original calendar below the Calendar column.
  3. Click Duplicate event and make any necessary changes.
  4. Click Save event.

 

Delete calendar events

You can delete a calendar event from the main Calendar tab or from a matter's calendar subtab. In a matter's calendar subtab, you can also bulk select and delete multiple events. Once an event is deleted, contact attendees will receive a notification of the change.

Important: You can only delete events from the calendar in which they were created. Additionally, you need appropriate permissions to delete events on calendars that are not your own. Learn more about permissions.
Calendar tab Matter's Calendar subtab
  1. Go to Calendar.
  2. Select the event on the relevant calendar. You can see which calendar the event belongs to when viewing the event modal.
  3. Click Delete.
  4. When the warning prompt appears, select Delete event.
  1. Go to the matter and click Calendar.
  2. Optional: Click Filters to filter the events.

  3. To delete a single event, click the down arrow next to Edit and select Delete. Or, to delete multiple events, use the check boxes to select all events you want to delete, then click Delete.

    Note: When you select an event that is part of a recurring series of events in order to delete it, only the selected event will be deleted. To delete recurring events, you have to do so from the main calendar tab.
  4. When the warning prompt appears, confirm the deletion(s).

 

Create, edit, and delete event types and colors

When creating a calendar event, you can create event types and also assign associated colors. When the event is saved, the main Calendar tab will show the event in the event type's color (with a small line on the left of the event showing the calendar's color). You will also see a colored circle in the event's title and description when viewing the calendar event as a line item in the matter's Calendar subtab.

Note: Event types can be used by all users on the firm account but only administrators can create, edit, and delete event types.

Important: If you change a color for an event type that has been applied on existing calendar events, all of those calendar events will retroactively change to the new color. This action is firm wide and will affect all firm users' calendar events using that color.

Create event type Change name and color Delete event type

Event type labels and associated colors are created in the New event or Edit event window of a calendar event. You can create your new event type labels by creating a new calendar event or editing an existing one from either the main Calendar tab or a matter's Calendar subtab. 

  1. Create an event or edit an existing event.
  2. In the New event or Edit event window, scroll down to Event types.
    • If no firm user on the account has created an event type, select Create event types and then click Add new. 
    • If there are one or more created event types, select the dropdown box, click Configure event types, and then click Add new. 
  3. Name the event type and select the colored circle to assign a color for the event type.
  4. Click Save. You can now add, replace, or remove the event type from the calendar event.

You can modify a previously created event type label by renaming it and by changing its color. Previously created event types can be modified in the New event or Edit event window of a calendar event. You can modify your existing event type labels by creating a new calendar event or editing an existing calendar event from either the main Calendar tab or a matter's Calendar subtab.

Note: Any changes made to event types will appear in the Dashboard Firm Feed.

  1. Create an event or edit an existing event.
  2. In the New event or Edit event window, scroll down to Event types.
  3. Under Event types, click the down arrow next to the search box and select Configure event types.
  4. Change the name and/or color of your event type(s).
  5. Click Save.

If you no longer need an existing event type, you can permanently delete it from your list of event types in the New event or Edit event window of a calendar event. You can delete event types by creating a new calendar event or editing an existing one from either the main Calendar tab or a matter's Calendar subtab.

  1. Create an event or edit an existing event.
  2. In the New event or Edit event window, scroll down to Event types.
  3. Under Event types, click the down arrow next to the search box and select Configure event types.
  4. Click the X next to an event type's name.
  5. When prompted to confirm the delete action, select Delete.
  6. Click Save.

 

Create recurring or repeating events

When creating a repeating calendar event, you can specify whether the event repeats daily, after a specific number of days, weekly, after a specific number of weeks, monthly, after a specific number of months, yearly, or after a specific number of years. You can also choose to never end the event, end after a certain number of events have happened, or end on a specific date. 

Note: Repeating events have a limit of 730 occurrences.

  1. Go to Calendar or the matter’s Calendar subtab and click New event. You can also click Create new and select Event.
  2. Complete the event details.
  3. Under Start time, check the box for Repeat.
  4. Specify the event repeat interval. After making a selection in the field next to Every, click any space outside the field to load the Summary at the bottom of the modal.
  5. Click Save.
  6. Click Save event.

 

Edit recurring events

Once a recurring event is created, you can edit any one of the recurring events, all recurring events, or only events after the selected event.

  1. Go to Calendar.
  2. Select the calendar that the event was created in.
  3. Click any one of the recurring events and select Edit event.
  4. Choose whether you want to edit this event, this event and the events following this one, or all events.
  5. Make your changes.
  6. Click Save event.

 

Delete recurring events

Once a recurring event is created, you can delete any one of the recurring events, all recurring events, or only events after the selected event.

  1. Go to Calendar.
  2. Select the calendar that the event was created in.
  3. Click any one of the recurring events and select Delete event.
  4. Choose whether you want to delete this event, this event and the events following this one, or all events.

 

Recover deleted events

If you deleted a calendar event in error, you can attempt recovery of the event from the Recovery bin.

Important: Attempting recovery of any deleted items is not guaranteed to be successful.
  1. Go to Settings > Recovery Bin.
  2. Click Filter.
  3. Under Type, select Calendar Entry and then click Search.
  4. Select Recover under the event.
  5. Select Ok.
