results.name: Create Matters
results.title: Create Matters
results.body:
In Clio Manage, you create a matter for every case your firm agrees to take on. Creating the matter means completing the matter form, the set of sections that capture everything the matter holds, from the client and matter details through to billing preferences and document folders. The same form reopens through Edit matter, and what you enter there populates the matter dashboard.

The form sections below follow the order in which they appear under the sections on the left when creating a matter. Sections tied to an add-on or a plan appear only for firms that have them.

Note: Role permissions can restrict a user's ability to create, edit, or view matters, and can limit access to specific matter details, documents, and communications.

Create matters

A matter always attaches to a contact. Link the matter to an existing contact or create a new contact before saving the matter. Clio Manage offers three places to start a new matter.

Note: From any of the three paths, click Save and run conflict check instead of Save matter to run a conflict check as part of creating the matter. Learn more about conflict checks in Clio Manage and Clio Grow.

Matters tab Create new button Contact card
  1. Go to Matters and click New Matter.
  2. Complete the matter form, working through the sections below.
  3. Click Save matter.
  1. Click Create new and select Matter.
  2. Complete the matter form, working through the sections below.
  3. Click Save matter.
  1. Go to Contacts and open a contact card. You can also search for the contact in the search bar.
  2. In the Client's matters section, click New matter.
  3. Complete the matter form, working through the sections below.
  4. Click Save matter.

 

Create placeholder matters

A placeholder matter is a temporary matter for tracking time spent on potential clients before your firm decides to represent them. Firms that prefer to wait for a signed engagement letter before opening a real matter can record that time against the placeholder, then move it once the letter arrives.

Tip: To bring matters in from another system, learn more about importing existing matters into Clio Manage. To turn a Clio Grow matter into a Clio Manage matter, learn more about converting matters from Clio Grow to Clio Manage.

  1. Create a company contact with your firm's name. Learn more about creating contacts.
  2. Create a new matter for that contact, using any of the three paths above.
    • Under Matter description, enter Placeholder.
  3. Add time entries to the placeholder matter. Learn more about time entries.
    • Under Description, enter the potential client's full name.
    • Under Matter, select the placeholder matter you created.
    • Complete the remaining time entry details as necessary.
  4. Once your firm decides to represent a potential client, create a matter for that client and move the time entries in bulk to the new matter.

 

Set up the matter

These four sections hold the core records of your case, such as who the client is, what kind of case it is, and who your firm is accountable for the legal matter. The fields here feed to the matters dashboard, matter stages, and reporting, so completing them accurately at the beginning of a case sets matters up for the lifecycle of your matters. You can use a matter template or an uploaded document to fill much of the matter form for you. 

Template information

Select an existing matter template to speed up matter creation. When an administrator sets a default template, its preset information automatically applies to the matter form. To use a different one, select it under Use an existing template. Any field the template fills stays editable. Learn more about matter templates.

 

Set up from documents

Upload or select existing documents to populate matter fields in the sections that follow. You can extract the information from engagement letters, retainer agreements, intake forms, email communications, and similar source documents to fill relevant matter fields. Only empty matter fields populate this way. Fields already filled by a matter template or by a third-party integration stay as they are. Extracted fields are highlighted in blue, so review the matter details afterward to confirm accuracy and completeness.

Use Upload new documents or Select documents in Clio to attach matter-related documents, up to five files per matter.

  • Supported formats: PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT, RTF, PNG, JPG.
  • Maximum file size: 15 MB per file.

Note: If the extraction finds several potential contacts, you will need to select which to add to the matter as clients and which to add as related contacts.

 

Client

You can add up to eleven clients to a matter. If you add more than one client, you will need to specify the default client. The default client becomes the primary contact and bill recipient. For multiple bill recipients, you can use split billing to preset the portion. You can also add non-client payers to a matter.

Note: Adding multiple clients is available on select plans. Learn more about your plan's features. To upgrade, ask a firm administrator.

 

Matter details

This section captures case-specific information. See below for a summary of unfamiliar fields.

Tip: When editing an existing matter, check Update matter name/number when saving changes at the top of the page to apply your firm's numbering scheme to the revised details. Learn more about the matter numbering scheme.

Responsible lawyer

The individual responsible for the matter.

Originating lawyer

The individual who brought the matter to the firm.

Responsible staff

An individual responsible for matter-related tasks beyond the responsible attorney. Automated workflows can use this field to assign task lists and tasks to that individual.

Client reference number

A tracking value of your firm's choosing, such as an internal reference number.

Location

The trial location, or the location of the incident.

Practice area

The type of case. Clio Manage arrives pre-populated with practice areas, and your firm can add its own. Learn more about Create and Manage Practice Areas. 

 

Set matter access and notifications

Setting permissions and blocking users are administrator controls, and blocking overrides group access. You can use matter permissions to maintain client privacy or block users' access if a conflict of interest arises. Matter notifications work the other way: you choose which firm users receive notifications, and each user controls which notification types they receive.  

Matter permissions

Select which firm users and groups have access to this matter. Selecting specific users or groups limits access to those users or groups. Learn more about setting matter permissions.

 

KYC checks

Know Your Client (KYC) information records the details of a risk assessment for a client's matter. What you log for the matter appears on the matter dashboard and on the dashboard of the primary contact associated with the matter.

You can add KYC information when creating a matter or when editing a matter. You can also add KYC information to a contact without tying it to a specific matter, in which case it stays off the matter dashboards for that contact. To keep KYC out of Clio Manage, leave the fields blank or disable the KYC field set.

 

Matter notifications

Firm users added to this section receive notifications when the matter is updated or deleted, when the matter budget is updated or crosses its threshold, and when the matter's trust balance falls below a specified threshold. Each user chooses which types to receive.

  1. Open the matter and scroll to the Matter notifications section.
  2. Under Firm user, search for a firm user.
  3. To remove a firm user, click the X beside their name.
  4. Click Save matter.

 

To change which notification types you receive:

  1. Go to Settings > Notifications.
  2. Scroll down to Matters.
  3. Toggle the relevant notification types on or off.

 

Block users

Administrators can block specific users from a matter, either one at a time or in bulk. Blocking users will restrict access where a conflict of interest exists. Unblocking is available at any time. Learn more about blocking users via permission settings.

Important: Blocking a user overrides group permissions. A user who belongs to a group with access to the matter loses that access once blocked, regardless of which groups they belong to.

Tip: Users with access to a matter can review its blocked users in the Timeline and Details sections of the matter's Dashboard, and in the Firm Feed.

  1. Create a new matter, or edit an existing matter.
  2. Scroll to the Block users section.
  3. Under Choose users to block, select the users to exclude from the matter.
  4. Click Save matter.

 

Add related contacts and custom fields

These two sections attach the people and the firm-specific data that sit alongside the client on a case. Both appear on the matter dashboard once saved, and both are available to any user who can edit the matter.

Related contacts

Related contacts are contacts connected to the matter but not represented by your firm, such as opposing counsel, witnesses, parents or guardians, siblings, spouses, children, and caretakers. Add a contact as a client only if they are employing your firm.

  1. Create a new matter, or edit an existing matter.
    • You can also click Add next to Related contacts on the matter's Dashboard.
  2. Scroll to the Related contacts section.
  3. Click Add related contact.
  4. Select the contact, or create a new one, and specify that contact's relationship to the matter.
  5. Optional: Check the box for Bill recipient.
  6. Click Save matter.

Custom fields

Custom fields are individualized fields of information relevant to a contact or a matter. Learn more about creating custom fields and field sets. Once created, the custom fields and field sets on a matter appear on the matter dashboard.

Note: Custom fields on the matter dashboard hold a fixed order, and the first twelve appear there.

  1. Open the matter and scroll to the Custom fields section.
  2. Click the Add a Custom Field or Custom Field set box and select a custom field or field set.
  3. Complete the custom field details.
  4. Optional: Click the X to remove a custom field or field set.

 

Set billing, attach records, and link conflict checks  

When creating a matter, you can set billing rates, fund allocation, assign task lists, and link conflict checks. Billing preference drives every activity, expense, and invoice on the matter, so confirm it before any time is recorded against the case. The Reports section is an administrator control, since it overrides a firm-wide setting. Personal injury preferences appear for firms with the Personal Injury add-on.

Billing preference

Specify the billing method for the matter. By default, a matter is billed at the hourly rate in your user profile. This section is where you set a different rate or set the matter to contingency or flat-fee billing. Learn more about the billing rate and activities hierarchy.

Note: If your firm uses multiple currencies and has conversion options enabled, your previous billing preferences may be affected. Learn more about multiple currencies in general bill settings.

  1. Open the matter and scroll to the Billing preference section.
  2. Select the invoice template.
  3. Check or clear This matter is billable.
    • A non-billable matter defaults its activities to zero, and those activities stay off bills.
    • To show a non-billable activity on the bill without charging the client, check both Non-billable and Show this entry on the bill when adding the time or expense entry.
  4. Under Billing method, select from the following options:
    • Hourly: When selecting hourly, you can set a custom billing rate in the Custom billing rates field.
    • Flat rate: When selecting flat rate, specify the Fee recipient and Amount. You can also choose a Flat fee category which will then populate the Amount field with the relevant value.
    • Contingency: When selecting contingency, specify the Fee recipient and enter the percentage of the award or settlement in the Rate field.
  5. Where applicable, choose the currency for the matter.
    • That currency applies to every activity, expense, invoice, and payment related to the matter.
    • Currencies added for your firm appear in this dropdown.
  6. Optional: Choose a Rate table and Rate category. Learn more about managing user rates with rate tables.
  7. Optional: Click Add a custom billing rate to override your personal rate for this matter.
  8. Optional: Click Set a budget for this matter, then select which firm users receive a notification when the matter reaches a budget threshold.
  9. Optional: Click Split the invoice for this matter, then click + Add payer. Under Payer, search for and select a contact, then under Invoice portion, set the percentage of the invoice total that bill recipients pay.
    • Optional: Click Send invoice copy to all bill recipients to include the payer when sending bills for this matter.
  10. Optional: Under Minimum required, enter a minimum trust balance for this matter to trigger a warning on the matter's financial dashboard. To allow automatic calculation and trust request generation, toggle Enable evergreen trust funds. Learn more about setting up evergreen trust.
  11. Optional: Under LEDES billing, select Enabled or Disabled to set whether UTBMS codes are required for time and expense entries on this matter. This section appears only where the matter's client has LEDES billing enabled.

 

Personal injury preferences

For firms with the Personal Injury add-on, this section sets preferences for personal injury cases, including whether legal fees deduct before or after expenses when determining a client's net compensation at settlement. Learn more about settlement.

  1. Open the matter and scroll to the Personal injury preferences section.
  2. Make any necessary changes.
  3. Click Save matter.

 

Task lists

You can add your task lists when creating a matter. Learn more about tasks and task lists.

  1. Open the matter and scroll to the Task lists section.
  2. Under Task list, select the list.
  3. Click Add task list to add another list.
  4. Optional: Click Notify assignees when these tasks are created to notify the firm user responsible for the task list. Learn more about adding assignees to task lists.
  5. Click Save matter.

 

Document folders

Create document folders during matter creation. Once created, the folders are available in the matter's Documents subtab, within the main Documents tab, and within the matter's folder in Clio Drive.

Note: Matter creation supports up to fifteen folders. Adding more document folders stays available after the matter exists.

  1. Open the matter and scroll to the Document folders section.
  2. Under Folder name, name the folder, then select the document category under Category.
    • Document categories group and sort documents and templates in Clio Manage. Learn more about document categories.
  3. Optional: Click Add a document folder to add another folder.
  4. Click Save matter.

 

Reports

Administrators can use this section to override the firm-wide originating and responsible attorney allocation for the fee allocation report on a single matter.

The fee allocation report covers the time and expenses each user has billed and collected for each matter, which helps determine a firm's bonus payout. Administrators set firm-wide percentages for how much of the collected time each originating and responsible attorney earns, and can override that firm-wide setting for individual matters. Reports generated previously keep their original allocations.

Note: Percentages set in the matter form apply to fee allocation reports for this matter alone. To set allocations at the firm level, administrators use reports permissions and settings.

  1. Open the matter and scroll to the Reports section.
  2. Firm-wide settings apply by default. To allocate percentages specific to this matter, clear the Use firm settings box. Each allocation carries its own checkbox.
  3. Enter a percentage under Originating lawyer allocation, Responsible lawyer allocation, or both.
  4. Optional: Click Add another user to add an additional user, their role, and the allocation for reporting purposes.
  5. Click Save matter.

 

Conflict checks

Link a conflict check that has already been run to this matter, so the check and its result stay with the case record. Learn more about conflict checks in Clio Manage and Clio Grow.

  1. Open the matter and scroll to the Conflict checks section.
  2. Under Conflict checks, select a conflict check.
  3. Optional: Click Link another conflict check to add another, or click the X to remove one.
  4. Click Save matter.

 

Up next

  • Change the matter later: Edit and Duplicate Matters. Reopen the matter form to update details, edit matters in bulk, or duplicate a matter as the basis for a new one.
  • Track the case as it progresses: Change Matter Statuses. Move a matter between open, pending, and closed.

results.title: Set Up Clio Accounting
results.body:
Clio Accounting is an accounting and bookkeeping tool built specifically for law firms. Clio Accounting connects your invoicing, payments, and accounting all in one place, allowing you to remain confident in your firm's compliance every step of the way. Not only is Clio Accounting built in consultation with accountants, but the simplified approach lets you get started right even if you may have a small firm with limited experience in the field of accounting. If you are a larger firm with specific accounting requirements, you can read through our Clio Accounting information to see if your firm may benefit from using it alongside your other Clio products.

With Clio Accounting you can

  • Connect bank accounts for automatic bank feed syncing, so transactions match to your books in almost real time instead of manual entry.

    Important: To sync the bank feed, your financial institution will need to support integration with Plaid. Contact your banking institution if you are not sure if your bank integrates with Plaid.
  • Get a firm-wide financial snapshot on the Dashboard, with accounts receivable, operating expenses, and profit and loss all in one view.
  • Rely on invoices and payments syncing automatically from Clio Manage, so journal entries are created for you instead of entered by hand.
US Canada

 

Sign in

While your firm needs a Clio Manage account to use Clio Accounting, not every user in Clio Accounting needs a Clio Manage account. How you sign in depends on if you have access to your firm's Clio Manage account.

Users with a Clio Manage account Users without a Clio Manage account
  1. Sign in to Clio Manage.
  2. In the upper left of the Clio Manage header, click Clio Manage and then select Clio Accounting.

Note: You can also sign in to Clio Accounting directly using the same email address and password you use for Clio Manage.  

  1. Go to Clio Accounting.
  2. Enter your email address and then click Next: Password.
  3. Enter your password and then click Sign In.

 

Complete the setup wizard

The first time someone with admin or accounts permissions signs in, Clio Accounting opens a welcome screen outlining what setup involves. Before continuing, make sure that your firm's address and currency is correct. Them click Get Started to begin the step through the pages. A bar at the top of each screen shows your progress through the pages.

  1. Set up your chart of accounts. Start from Clio's pre-built chart of accounts for legal professionals, or import your existing one from a CSV file if you are moving from another bookkeeping tool. See Clio Accounting: Set up Chart of Accounts for more information.
  2. Assign Clio Manage transactions. Choose which of your Clio Manage operating and trust accounts to bring into Clio Accounting. You need to select at least one operating account.
  3. Set an accounting start date. Choose the date your bookkeeping records begin in Clio Accounting. Clio uses this date to set your opening balances and to decide how far back to import your Clio Manage transactions.
  4. Add Canadian tax authorities. In Canada, you are also asked to assign a tax authority to each of your tax rates before continuing. Make sure to first  create your tax rates and choose the appropriate tax authorities for each rate in Clio Manage to set these up, or edit them if you previously created tax rates.

Click Finish setup to complete setup. Clio Accounting then opens on the Dashboard, where a short tour and a list of recommended tasks help you pick up the remaining setup work, such as connecting a bank account and setting your trust account opening balances.
 

 

Invite new users

Managing access to Clio Accounting allows you to collaborate securely with your team or external bookkeepers on your firm's financial records. By assigning specific user roles, you can ensure that sensitive financial data is only accessible to authorized personnel while maintaining an accurate audit trail of all accounting activities. You will learn how to invite existing Clio Manage users or external accountants to your bookkeeping workspace.

Note: Only the Primary Subscriber has the authority to invite users, resend pending invitations, or deactivate accounting access.
Invite an existing Clio Manage user Invite a new user
  1. Go to Settings and click Invite user.
  2. Select Invite an existing Clio Manage user option.

  3. Click the down arrow next to the Full name field and choose a name from the list. 

    Note: Clio Manage users who don't have admin or accounts permissions can use Clio Accounting features after Clio Accounting setup is complete, but they won't be able to complete Clio Accounting setup. 

  4. Choose the user type.
    • Accountant/Bookkeeper: For individuals responsible for daily accounting tasks, reconciliations, and financial reporting.
    • Standard: For firm members who need to view accounting data but may not perform specialized bookkeeping actions.
  5. Click Send invite.
  1. Go to Settings and click Invite user.
  2. Select Invite a user without Clio Manage access option.
  3. Fill the user details and choose the appropriate user type.
    • Accountant/Bookkeeper: For individuals responsible for daily accounting tasks, reconciliations, and financial reporting.
    • Standard: For firm members who need to view accounting data but may not perform specialized bookkeeping actions.
  4. Click Send invite.

 

Resend or revoke user invites

Resend invite Revoke invite
  1. Go to Settings.
  2. For the relevant user with a Invitation sent status, click the more icon (ellipses) in the Actions column.
  3. Select Resend invite.
  1. Go to Settings.
  2. For the relevant user with a Invitation sent status, click the more icon (ellipses) in the Actions column.
  3. Select Cancel invite, then click Cancel invite when the warning appears.

 

Deactivate or reactivate users

Deactivate invite Reactiate invite
  1. Go to Settings.
  2. For the relevant user with an Active status, click the more icon (ellipses) in the Actions column.
  3. Select Deactivate.
  4. Click Deactivate user.
  1. Go to Settings.
  2. For the relevant user with an Disabled status, click the more icon (ellipses) in the Actions column.
  3. Select Reactivate.
  4. Review that the information is accurate, then click Send invite.

 

Log out

You can log out of Clio Accounting from the main navigation menu. Logging out will also log you out of Clio Manage and Clio Grow.

  1. In the left navigation menu, click Logout.

results.title: Clio for Clients: Law Firm Actions
results.body:
Send messages or documents

With Clio for Clients, you can send your clients messages and share documents or folders via the Clio Manage web or mobile app. Your client will be notified when you share documents or folders with them via their client portal. You and other members in your firm can also receive in-app and/or email notifications when your client responds or uploads a document in their client portal. Only one notification will be sent for client portal events that occur within a one-minute time frame. Notification settings can be managed in Settings > Client portal messages.

Send message and document Send existing document

Follow the directions below to send a document when composing a message.

  1. Go to the matter’s Communications subtab and click Go to client portal.
  2. Select the Messages subtab.
  3. Click Attach a document to add a resource, type a message, and click Send. If you need to share multiple documents at once, you can also share a whole document folder.
  4. Click the Shares resources subtab to view shared documents.

Note: The maximum file size upload in the client portal is 100MB.

Follow the directions below to share an existing document or entire document folder in Clio Manage.

  1. Go to the main Documents tab or the Documents subtab within a matter.
  2. Click the arrow beside View and select Share to client portal.

 

Client invitation email

After sending your first message or sharing an initial document resource, your client will receive an email invitation to join Clio for Clients. This email will contain your firm’s logo and name and a sign in link which remains valid for one hour. When the link expires, your client can enter their email address into the portal sign in page to request a new link to be sent to their email address.

Your firm controls the email address that the invitation email is sent to. Your client can only access the client portal using this email address. By default, the contact’s primary email address is selected. If there is no designated primary email address, the email will be sent to the client’s first listed email address. Administrators can change this by updating the Clio for Clients email field when they edit a contact in Clio Manage.

 

Share documents or folders

You can share multiple documents via the client portal.

  1. In a Matter, select the Documents subtab.
  2. Use the checkboxes to select the documents you want to share.
  3. Click Actions > Share to client portal.
  4. Add a message to your client, then click Share.

To help keep track of the documents your client has access to via the client portal, you can share a folders with them.

Note: Documents added to previously shared folders will automatically be shared with clients. This means that if you share a folder with a client and then later add more documents to the folder, your client will have access to all the documents in the folder, including the recently added documents.

Tip: To keep track of the documents your client shares with you via the client portal, you can create and share a folder specifically for client uploads. Use an intuitive name for the folder like "Client uploads", and when you share the folder, add a message to your client so that they understand the purpose of this folder.

  1. In a Matter, select the Documents subtab.
  2. For the folder that you want to share, click the down arrow next to Edit and select Share to client portal.
  3. Optional: Add a message.
  4. Click Share.

 

Show all client portal events

When viewing the Messages subtab of a client portal, you can choose to show or hide client portal events including when participants read messages and documents, when participants were added or removed, when participants changed the email address used to sign in to the client portal, and (if enabled) when a matter moves to a new stage. These client portal events will appear in the message feed with a timestamp indicating when the participant completed the action.

  1. Go to the matter’s Communications subtab and click Go to client portal.
  2. Select the Messages subtab.
  3. Toggle on or off Show all client portal events. 

 

Stop sharing documents

You can stop document share in either the client portal or the matter’s Documents subtab.

Client portal Documents subtab
  1. Go to the matter’s Communications subtab and click Go to client portal.
  2. Select the Shared resources subtab.
  3. Click the down arrow next to View and click Stop sharing.
  1. Go to the matter’s Documents subtab.
  2. Click the down arrow next to View and click Stop sharing to client portal.

 

Send bills and matter trust requests

When sending bills to clients, you can send bills and matter trust requests by email, through Clio for Clients if your clients have active client portals, or both. Your client will receive an email notification informing them of the bill. Once a bill is shared, both you and your client can view the bill in the client portal at any time. Changes made to the bill will immediately reflect in the client portal, which means that you will not need to re-share the bill by email. 

You can send bills and matter trust requests either individually or in bulk through the client portal. If you share a bill via Clio for Clients, your client can access the bill from an email notification or from within the client portal. If your firm has Clio Payments enabled, your client can also pay their bill by clicking the payment link in the email or by accessing the client portal.

Note: The option to send a bill through the client portal will only appear if a client portal is set up prior to sending the bill. If your client does not have an active client portal, see this article to learn more about getting started.

Important: You cannot share multi-matter bills (bills containing activities from multiple matters for a single contact) and contact-level trust requests through Clio for Clients. If these bills are included when sending bills in bulk, they will be sent by email only. Supported bills and matter-level trust requests will be sent via the client portal. 

Share one bill Share multiple bills
  1. Go to Billing or go to the Bills subtab within the matter.
  2. Find the bill you want to send and click Send.
  3. In the send bill modal, toggle on Send to client portal.
  4. Optional: Add a message to your client. Your client will see this message in the email notification.
  5. Optional: Toggle on Send via email to also send the bill by email.
  6. Click Send bill.
  1. Go to Billing or go to the Bills subtab within the matter.
  2. Check the boxes for the bills you want to send and then click Send.
  3. In the send bill modal, toggle on Send to client portal.
  4. Optional: Add a message to your clients. Your clients will see this message in the email notification.
  5. Optional: Toggle on Send via email to also send the bill by email.
  6. Click For client portal contacts or For email contacts in the bill preview window on the right to see which bills will be sent through the client portal and which bills will be sent by email.
  7. Click Send items.

 

Share calendar events

When you create a calendar event in Clio Manage and add a client with an active client portal as an event attendee, you can share the event via Clio for Clients, allowing your client to access all collaboration between them and your firm in one place. This option is selected by default if your client has a client portal. Once the event is shared, your client will receive a notification in Clio for Clients and an email notification of the event. Learn how clients view shared events in the client portal, including the difference between the My events and Case events tabs.

Important: When you share a calendar event to a client portal, the event is visible to every client in that portal, including clients who were not invited as attendees to the calendar event. Clients who were invited as event attendees see the full event details, and clients who were not invited see limited details. If a portal includes more than one client and you do not want all of them to see an event, do not share the event to the portal.

Learn how to invite attendees and notify them via Clio for Clients when you create a calendar event. You can also uninvite attendees when you edit a calendar event.

 

Share client portal login link

You can embed a public link on your website that your clients can click to access the client portal. You can also share this link directly with your clients.

Note: Your clients can only log in to their client portals using this link if they have already created Clio for Clients accounts.

  1. Copy this link: https://clients.clio.com/login.  
  2. Send this link in a message, email, or embed it on your website.

 

Revoke access to client portals

Once opened, a client portal cannot be deleted or closed, but you can revoke access to individual items or the entire portal. You can delete a message in the portal, stop sharing resources (see above section), or remove a participant.

Delete message Remove participant
  1. Go to the matter’s Communications subtab and click Go to client portal.
  2. Find the message under the Messages subtab and click the trash can icon when hovering over the message.
  3. When prompted to confirm, click Delete message.
  1. Go to the matter’s Communications subtab and click Go to client portal.
  2. Under Participants, hover over a participant’s name and click the X icon.
  3. When prompted to confirm, click Remove.

results.name: Edit and Delete Contacts
results.title: Edit and Delete Contacts
results.body:
In Clio Manage, you can edit contacts one at a time, convert a contact between the person and company types on the same form, and delete contacts your firm no longer needs. Current contact records let you send bills to the right client, keep matter numbering accurate, and rely on your conflict check results. Deleting a contact releases its notes, client portal, and Clio for Co-Counsel access, while bills, matters, transactions, and payments stay in Clio Manage without a contact attached.

Tip: Click Recents in the Clio Manage header to return to a contact you worked on recently.

Edit a contact

If you update a client name and the matter numbering for that client's matters contains the name, edit those matters so the numbering matches. Refer to Edit and Duplicate Matters.

Note: If your firm uses QuickBooks Online and contact information returns after you save your changes, remove that information in QuickBooks Online first.

Change contact information

  1. In Clio Manage, click Contacts, then click Edit beside the contact name. You can also search for the contact, open the record, then click Edit contact.
  2. Make your changes.
  3. Click Save contact.

 

Change a contact type between person and company

Clio Manage provides two base contact types, and you can convert a contact from one to the other at any time. 

  1. In Clio Manage, click Contacts, then click Edit beside the contact name.
  2. Select Person or Company.
  3. Click Save contact.
    • Converting a contact to a company adds the Employees section to the record, where you link the person contacts who work there.

 

Understand what deletion removes

Review what a deletion affects before you remove a contact, because the outcome depends on which route you use. You can view a record of which user deleted each contact from the Firm Feed on your Clio Manage dashboard.

Released with contact

Contact notes, client portal access, and Clio for Co-Counsel access.

Retained in Clio Manage

Bills, matters, transactions, and payments. These records remain in your account without a contact attached.

Recoverable for six months

Contacts deleted from a contact record or from the contacts table. Refer to Recover Deleted Contacts.

Permanent

Contacts deleted with the bulk operations tool. Confirm your selection in the preview before you run the operation.

 

Delete contacts

Choose the route that matches how many contacts you are removing and whether you need the deletion to stay reversible.

Single Contact Multiple Contacts Bulk Contacts
  1. In Clio Manage, click Contacts, then click Edit beside the contact name. You can also search for the contact, open the record, then click Edit contact.
  2. Click Delete contact.
  3. Select the check box to confirm the action, then click Delete contact.

Users with administrator permissions can remove several contacts at once from the contacts table.

  1. In Clio Manage, click Contacts.
  2. Select the checkbox next to each contact you want to remove.
  3. Click Delete contacts.
  4. Select the check box to confirm the action, then click Delete contact.

Administrators and the primary subscriber can use the bulk operations tool to clear all contacts from the account or remove identical duplicates. To access the bulk operations page, use the link provided in step 2.

Remove Duplicate Contacts applies to identical duplicates. Duplicate contacts associated with matters, related matters, employees, transactions, notes, or communications remain in your account, and you can combine those records manually instead.

Important: Contacts removed via the bulk operations tool remain deleted. The Recovery Bin does not retain them. Review the preview in step 7 before you confirm.

  1. Log in to Clio Manage as an administrator.
  2. Open the bulk operations page for your region:
    • US
    • EU
    • Canada
  3. Click Add.
  4. Select Remove ALL Contacts or Remove Duplicate Contacts.
  5. Optional: Select Exclude clients to keep contacts that have matters.
  6. Click Generate Preview, then wait for State to change from Preview Queued to Preview Completed.
  7. Click Preview and review the entries listed for deletion.
  8. Click Confirm Deletion.
  9. Click Perform Operation.
  10. Click OK in the warning window to start the deletion.

 

Up next

  • Recover Deleted Contacts: Restore a contact deleted in error within six months.

results.name: Create and Manage Expenses Entries
results.title: Create and Manage Expenses Entries
results.body:
Expense entries in Clio Manage allow you to track and recover costs related to your matters, such as court filing fees and travel expenses. By default, all expenses are recorded as standard expenses without categorisation. If your firm needs to differentiate between expenses paid to third parties (hard costs) and internal costs billed to clients (soft costs), you can enable these options in Settings. If your firm uses the Xero integration, you can also track the real-time payment status of these expenses directly within Clio Manage.

Enable expense tracking for hard and soft costs

By default, Clio Manage does not track expenses as hard costs vs soft costs. If your firm needs to track expenses this way, you can enable this setting.

Important: If you do not enable this setting tracking, all expenses are categorized as standard expenses without categorization options.

  1. Go to Settings > Billing.
  2. Select the Expenses subtab.
  3. Toggle Soft and hard costs for expenses.
    • Your changes will save automatically.

Tip: If your firm uses Clio Accounting, hard costs recorded in Clio Manage are synced to Clio Accounting. You can view your hard costs as a single table in the main Hard costs tab in Clio Accounting.

 

Enable linking hard costs to bank transactions

With this feature, you can enable linking hard costs to bank transactions.

  1. Go to Settings > Billing > Expenses.

  2. Toggle on Link hard costs to bank transactions.

    Note: To toggle Link hard costs to bank transactions, you will first need to toggle Soft and hard costs for expenses to on.

 

Add new expenses

Expenses track costs related to a matter in Clio Manage. Record these costs and attach receipts to facilitate firm reimbursement and provide clients with clear bill transparency. You can create expense entries from several areas in Clio Manage, including the main Activities page, a matter’s Activities subtab, or the global Create new button.

Important: The auto-fill expense entries feature is in pilot. Auto-fill expense entries in Clio will extract and auto-fill key information into the amount, date, reference fields, and extract a brief description of your receipts. Autofill only applies to empty fields.
Note: When recording soft costs, you can enter up to four decimal places. Other areas in Clio may round values to two decimal places, but the actual rate remains unchanged. Quick bills support two decimal places. 
  1. In Activities, click New expense.
    • Alternatively, from the global Create new button, select Expense entry.

  2. If you previously enabled tracking expenses as Hard costs or Soft costs, choose the relevant option.

    Note: Learn how to link transactions to hard costs when you record a transaction.

  3. Optional: In the Receipt section, click Attach receipt and select a file from Clio of upload one from your computer.

    Tip: With Clio's AI features, you can allow Clio to extract relevant information from the attached file to auto-fill fields in the modal.
    • You can select up to five files to associate with the expense entry.
    • To update the modal fields with values extracted from the last attached file, click Autofill with latest receipt.
    • To remove an expense receipt from the form, click the X button. Removing an expense receipt detaches it from the expense.

    • To include attached receipts on client bills, check the Send receipt with bill box.

      Note: Receipts attached to non-billable expenses will not be sent with the bill.

  4. Optional: Under Expense category, select a pre-created category to auto-populate certain fields. If the matter has LEDES billing enabled, select the relevant code under UTBMS expense code. For the Tax field, choose one of your pre-created tax rates.

    Note: The rate(s) added here are used as the default tax rates, but you can still edit them at the time you generate a bill.
  5. If your firm uses multiple currencies and the expense currency is different from the matter’s currency, you may have to select the conversion rate to use (if you chose Billing Settings where the rate is set at the time you record the expense).
  6. Complete the remaining fields.
    • When entering the date, you can select a past, current, or future date.

    • You can mark an expense as non-billable by checking the Non-billable box. If you still want the non-billable expense to appear on bills, check the Show this entry on the bill box.

      Note: Tracking non-billable expenses helps the firm track non-billable activities and report on non-billable time using the Matter productivity by user report. Showing these entries on bills demonstrates the extra value invested in a client's matter.
      Important: Non-billable expenses marked as Show on bill will only appear on bills generated using bulk billing (Billing > New bills). They will not appear on invoices generated using Quick bill.
    • Optional: Select a tax rate or rates to apply to the expense. You have to create the tax rate first in order to select it from the dropdown when you create an expense entry.
      • When selecting multiple rates you can apply subsequent taxes to the pre- or post-tax amount.
  7. Save the entry.
    • Click Save entry to save and exit the modal.
    • Click Save and > Create another to save the entry and clear the fields in the modal to create another entry.
    • Click Save and > Duplicate to save the entry and keep the fields filled to create additional similar entries.

 

Track vendor bill status

If your firm uses the Xero integration with the Sync to Xero as bills to pay setting enabled, you can monitor the real-time sync status of your Hard costs and Anticipated disbursements.

Tip: Tracking the Vendor bill status ensures all firm-paid expenses are accounted for before you finalize a client bill. This helps protect firm cash flow by ensuring you don't overlook unpaid liabilities.

  1. Go to the main Activities tab or the Activities subtab within a specific matter.
  2. Locate the Hard cost entry.
  3. View the Vendor bill status field:
    • Hard costs: These entries sync to Xero as Paid bills, as they represent expenses already settled by the firm.
    • Anticipated disbursements: These entries sync to Xero as Unpaid bills. The status updates to Paid once you link a bank transaction to the entry in Clio Manage.

Note: Xero does not allow edits to paid bills. Once an entry is marked as Paid, it becomes read-only in Clio Manage and cannot be edited or reverted to Unpaid.

 

Duplicate and edit expenses

You can edit and duplicate an expense activity from the main Activities page in Clio Manage or from the Activities subtab within a matter. 

Duplicate expenses Edit expenses
  1. Go to Activities and find the expense you want to duplicate.
  2. In the Actions column, click Duplicate, or select Duplicate from the dropdown.
  3. Make any necessary changes.
  4. Click Save entry.

You can edit an unbilled expense to update details such as the amount, billable status or description.

  1. Go to Activities and find the expense you want to duplicate.
  2. In the Actions column, click Edit, or select Edit from the dropdown
  3. Make any necessary changes.
  4. Click Save entry.

 

Delete and recover expenses

You can delete an unbilled expense from the main Activities page in Clio Manage or from the Activities subtab within a matter and administrators can recover expenses from the Recovery Bin. You can also track deleted expenses in the Recovery Bin, a matter timeline, and from the Firm Feed in your dashboard.

Important: Deleted expenses remain in the Recovery Bin for six months and can usually be restored, but Clio does not guarantee data recovery. Users can delete individual expenses and  administrators can delete multiple expenses at the same time.
Delete a single expense Delete multiple expenses Recover expenses
  1. Go to Activities.
  2. In the Actions column, click Delete or select Delete from the dropdown. You can also check the box next to the expense you want to delete, then click Delete above the table header.
  3. When the warning prompt appears, select Delete entry.
  1. Go to Activities, then select the Expense filter.
  2. Select the checkbox in the table header to select all expense activities.
  3. Click Delete.
  4. When the warning prompt appears, click Delete entries to confirm the action.
  1. Go to Settings > Recovery Bin.
  2. Click Filter and search by Activity.
  3. For the relevant entry, click Recover to attempt recovery.
